title: Integrity of Tumor Cytokine Sensing as a Determinant of Durable Benefit from PD-1 Blockade

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Durable benefit from PD-1 blockade is confined to a minority of patients, and a substantial fraction of initial responders progress after one to three years of disease control. Tumor-intrinsic responsiveness to IFN-gamma released by activated CD8 T cells is a plausible rate-limiting step: signaling through IFNGR1, IFNGR2, JAK1, JAK2 and STAT1 drives surface MHC class I, PD-L1, and the CXCL9 and CXCL10 chemokines that recruit further effector cells. We propose that truncating and missense inactivation of JAK1 or JAK2, together with promoter methylation of downstream response elements, is a principal route by which melanoma and lung tumors escape after an initial radiographic response. Using 220 paired pre-treatment and progression biopsies from patients treated with pembrolizumab or nivolumab, genome-scale CRISPR screens under cytokine selection, and syngeneic models, we will map pathway lesions, establish causality, and test innate-agonist and NK-redirection strategies that restore killing when tumor cytokine sensing is lost.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Define the spectrum and clonal timing of IFN-gamma pathway lesions. We will perform whole-exome and RNA sequencing on 220 paired biopsies and use single-cell copy-number inference to determine whether JAK1 and JAK2 lesions are pre-existing subclones or emerge under treatment pressure. Aim 2. Establish causality and identify bypass nodes. Isogenic JAK1-null, JAK2-null and STAT1-null lines derived from patient tumors will be scored for MHC class I induction, CXCL9 secretion, and susceptibility to autologous T cell killing; a genome-scale CRISPR activation screen will nominate nodes that force surface antigen display without upstream receptor signaling. Aim 3. Test therapeutic bypass in vivo. In B16-F10 and MC38 derivatives engineered for pathway loss we will evaluate STING agonism, NKG2D-engaging bispecifics, and TNF-driven killing combined with anti-PD-1, using survival and intratumoral immune composition as endpoints.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Approximately 25 to 40 percent of melanoma patients who achieve an objective response to PD-1 blockade eventually progress, and the biology of that escape is far less well characterized than the determinants of initial benefit. Because tumor cytokine sensing controls both antigen display and chemokine-mediated effector recruitment, its loss simultaneously disables recognition and infiltration, producing a lesion that is invisible rather than merely tolerated. Distinguishing tumors that lack signaling capacity from those that retain it but are restrained by suppressive stroma is clinically consequential: the former will not benefit from any agent that works by amplifying T cell effector output, whereas the latter may. This project will supply the genetic and functional criteria needed to make that distinction at progression and will nominate the first mechanistically matched salvage strategies for the signaling-null subset.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Prior reports describe individual patients carrying JAK1 or JAK2 mutations at relapse but have not established how often such lesions are pre-existing subclones rather than treatment-selected, nor whether pathway loss can be therapeutically circumvented. Three features are new. First, the paired-biopsy cohort is powered to resolve subclonal fractions below two percent using duplex-barcoded sequencing, which converts an anecdotal observation into a quantitative model of selection. Second, we use CRISPR activation rather than knockout screening to search for routes that force surface antigen display downstream of the receptor, an approach not previously applied to escape biology. Third, every genomic finding is paired with an autologous killing assay using expanded tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes from the same patient, so functional consequence is measured in the patient-specific antigen context rather than inferred from cell line surrogates.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Patients receiving pembrolizumab or nivolumab at three centers will undergo protocol biopsies at baseline and at radiographic progression under NCT03521739; 220 evaluable pairs are projected over four years. Sequencing uses a 512-gene duplex panel plus whole-exome and bulk RNA with matched normal for germline subtraction. Pathway status will be scored by an integrated call combining mutation, copy number, promoter methylation, and a 12-gene induction module measured after ex vivo cytokine exposure of short-term cultures. With 220 pairs and an assumed 12 percent lesion frequency at progression versus 3 percent at baseline, power is 88 percent at two-sided alpha 0.05. Preclinical work uses B16-F10 and MC38 with CRISPR-engineered Jak1 or Jak2 deletion implanted in C57BL/6 mice, ten animals per arm, analyzed by mixed-effects growth models and log-rank tests.

title: TREM2-Expressing Macrophage Programs That Enforce Failure of Checkpoint Blockade

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Tumors that fail PD-1 blockade despite abundant T cell infiltration are frequently dominated by a conserved macrophage state marked by TREM2, APOE, SPP1, C1QC and lipid-handling genes. We hypothesize that this state is not a passive marker of failure but an active enforcer: TREM2 signaling through DAP12 stabilizes a program that consumes arginine, secretes TGFB1 and IL10, and physically sequesters CD8 cells at the invasive margin, so that infiltrating lymphocytes lose polyfunctional cytokine co-production and cytolytic granule release. Using single-cell and spatial profiling of 180 pre-treatment and on-treatment human tumors, TREM2 germline deletion and antibody blockade in syngeneic models, and adoptive transfer of congenically marked T cells, we will define the trajectory of this macrophage state, test its causal contribution, and determine whether its removal restores sensitivity to anti-PD-1 in otherwise refractory tumors.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Map macrophage state trajectories across treatment. Single-cell RNA sequencing with paired TCR capture on 180 biopsies from melanoma, renal and lung cohorts will define state abundance before and during therapy and test association with best overall response by RECIST. Aim 2. Determine causality using genetic and antibody-mediated TREM2 removal. Trem2 knockout and knockout bone marrow chimeras implanted with MC38, B16-F10 and LLC will be compared with wild-type recipients for tumor growth, and a depleting anti-TREM2 monoclonal will be tested for pharmacodynamic collapse of the state. Aim 3. Establish whether state removal restores CD8 effector function and sensitizes to PD-1 blockade. We will quantify granzyme B release, TNF and IFN-gamma co-production, and clonal replacement of transferred OT-I cells, and evaluate anti-TREM2 plus anti-PD-1 combinations for durable rejection and rechallenge immunity.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Most translational effort in checkpoint biology has focused on lymphocytes, yet mononuclear phagocytes are the most abundant hematopoietic population in the majority of solid tumors and are the principal source of the metabolic and cytokine constraints that lymphocytes encounter. The TREM2-marked state recurs across cancer types and across species, which argues that it is a stereotyped tissue program rather than a tumor-specific artifact. If this program is causally upstream of T cell dysfunction, it defines a target class that is genetically stable, unlike tumor cells themselves, and therefore less likely to be lost under therapeutic selection. Establishing causality is a precondition for the rational design of combination trials, several of which are already proceeding on correlative association alone and risk failing for lack of a pharmacodynamic endpoint.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: We combine three elements that have not previously been used together. First, paired single-cell transcriptome and receptor sequencing on serial human biopsies allows macrophage state abundance to be linked to the fate of individual expanded T cell clones in the same specimen rather than to bulk composition. Second, we use a depleting rather than a signaling-blocking antibody, which distinguishes loss of the receptor from loss of the cell and resolves an ambiguity that has confounded prior work. Third, we developed a bone marrow chimera system in which only the phagocyte compartment lacks the receptor, allowing separation of intratumoral from systemic contributions. The pharmacodynamic readout, a six-gene module measurable in a 50-cell needle aspirate, is designed for direct transfer into early-phase trials.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Human specimens come from an existing biobank with linked outcomes under NCT02857933 and from prospective accrual at two sites. Single-cell libraries will be generated with 5-prime chemistry, targeting 6000 cells per sample; state assignment uses a reference-projection model with bootstrap confidence and is validated by multiplexed immunofluorescence on serial sections. Association testing uses mixed-effects logistic regression with tumor type as a random effect; with 180 samples and an expected 30 percent response rate we can detect an odds ratio of 2.4 per interquartile increase in state abundance with 85 percent power. Mouse experiments use ten animals per arm with prespecified growth-curve mixed models, and all antibody studies include isotype and Fc-silent controls to separate depletion from blockade.

title: Organized Lymphoid Aggregates and Intratumoral B Cell Immunity as Determinants of Checkpoint Blockade Benefit

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Solid tumors that respond to PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade frequently contain organized aggregates of CD20-positive B cells surrounded by CD3-positive T cell zones, follicular dendritic cell networks marked by CD21 and CD23, and PNAd-positive high endothelial venules. These structures resemble secondary lymphoid organs and appear to support local priming, affinity maturation and antibody production. We propose that their maturation stage, not their mere presence, determines clinical benefit, and that immature aggregates lacking germinal center reactions are prognostically inert. This project will quantify aggregate maturation in 400 archival specimens from melanoma, sarcoma and renal cell carcinoma treated with checkpoint blockade, determine the cellular composition and clonal architecture of the B cells within them, and test in mouse models whether LTA and LTB dependent induction of these structures converts non-responding tumors into responders.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Establish a reproducible maturation grade. Using multiplex immunofluorescence and whole-slide analysis we will grade aggregates as early, primary follicle-like, or germinal center containing based on CD21, CD23, Ki-67 and AID staining, and relate grade to overall survival in 400 treated specimens. Aim 2. Define the B cell repertoire and function within graded aggregates. Laser capture and paired heavy and light chain sequencing will test whether aggregate-resident B cells are clonally expanded and somatically mutated, and whether their secreted immunoglobulin binds autologous tumor lysate. Aim 3. Test causality and induction. In LTBR-blocked and B cell-depleted mice bearing MC38 and YUMMER1.7 tumors, and in animals treated with an LIGHT-based vascular targeting agent, we will determine whether structure formation is required for and sufficient to improve response to anti-PD-1.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Clinical biomarker development for checkpoint blockade has concentrated on tumor cell properties and on cytotoxic lymphocyte density, both of which perform inconsistently across disease sites. The organized lymphoid compartment offers a different axis of information because it reports on the capacity of the tumor bed to sustain local immune reactions rather than on the current level of infiltration. Sarcoma is a particularly informative setting because overall response rates to PD-1 blockade are low, yet a reproducible minority of patients achieve prolonged control, and that minority is enriched for the structures we propose to grade. A validated maturation grade would provide an assay that is inexpensive, performed on standard formalin-fixed tissue, and interpretable by a pathologist without specialized instrumentation.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Most published work scores these structures as present or absent on hematoxylin and eosin sections, a binary that mixes biologically distinct entities and explains much of the inconsistency in the literature. We introduce a four-marker maturation grade with prespecified thresholds and an interobserver reliability study across six pathologists. We also introduce paired repertoire sequencing from microdissected aggregates, which allows us to ask whether the humoral response is tumor-directed rather than bystander. Finally, we use a vascular targeting agent to induce structures pharmacologically, converting a correlative observation into an interventional hypothesis. The combination of a deployable grading assay, a functional repertoire readout, and a pharmacological induction strategy distinguishes this proposal from descriptive spatial pathology efforts.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Archival blocks come from three completed trials and two institutional registries with a median follow-up of 46 months. Whole-slide multiplex panels will be run in a single batch with tissue microarray controls; grading is performed blinded to outcome, with 60 slides double-read for reliability, targeting a Fleiss kappa above 0.70. Survival analysis uses Cox models stratified by disease site and adjusted for stage, prior therapy, and lymphocyte density; with 400 specimens and 55 percent event rate we have 80 percent power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.63 for high-grade versus low-grade aggregates. Mouse studies use ten animals per arm, with structure quantification on serial sections by an investigator blinded to treatment assignment.

title: Comparative and Combined Predictive Value of PD-L1 Tumor Proportion Score, Tumor Mutational Burden and Mismatch Repair Status

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Three assays are used to select patients for PD-1 blockade: immunohistochemical PD-L1 tumor proportion score, tumor mutational burden measured by sequencing, and mismatch repair or microsatellite instability status. They are frequently treated as interchangeable, yet they measure different biology and are only weakly correlated with one another. We propose a prospective-retrospective program to determine the independent and joint predictive value of the three measures in a harmonized multi-cohort framework. We will assemble 1400 patients treated with pembrolizumab, nivolumab or atezolizumab across lung, gastroesophageal, colorectal and urothelial primaries, generate all three assays centrally on the same tissue block, and model objective response and progression-free survival with prespecified interaction terms. The deliverable is a calibrated multivariable selection rule with decision-curve analysis, plus a public reference set of tissue and matched sequencing data for future assay comparisons.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Generate harmonized central assays. All 1400 blocks will be stained for PD-L1 with the 22C3 and SP263 clones, sequenced on a 468-gene panel with matched normal, and tested for mismatch repair protein loss by immunohistochemistry and by an NGS microsatellite classifier. Aim 2. Estimate independent predictive value. Logistic and Cox models with treatment interaction terms will quantify the contribution of each measure to objective response and progression-free survival, with prespecified subgroup analyses by primary site and line of therapy. Aim 3. Build and validate a combined selection rule. A penalized regression model will be fit in a 900-patient training set and locked before evaluation in a 500-patient held-out set, with calibration, net reclassification, and decision-curve analyses reported. We will additionally quantify how frequently the three assays disagree in individual patients and characterize the discordant groups.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Selection decisions made with a single assay misclassify a large minority of patients in both directions. Roughly 15 percent of lung tumors scoring below one percent by immunohistochemistry nevertheless achieve durable responses, while a comparable fraction of high-scoring tumors progress at first assessment. Because the three measures capture partially independent axes of biology, the amount of antigenic material available for recognition, the local adaptive signal that induces ligand expression, and the specific hypermutator process that generates frameshift-derived epitopes, combining them should outperform any one alone. No adequately powered study has generated all three assays centrally on the same tissue in a multi-tumor population, which is why current guidelines rest on cross-trial comparison rather than on direct within-patient contrasts.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: The innovation is methodological rather than mechanistic. First, all assays are generated centrally on the same block, eliminating the tissue-heterogeneity confound that dominates published comparisons. Second, the analytic plan is locked and registered before any outcome data are unblinded, and the validation set is physically sequestered. Third, we evaluate assays with decision-curve analysis rather than with area under the curve alone, so that results are expressed in terms of the clinical consequence of acting on the test at a stated threshold. Fourth, we will release deidentified image tiles, sequencing data and outcomes as a reference resource, which converts a single study into a standing benchmark against which future assays and computational classifiers can be compared without re-accrual.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Cases are drawn from four institutional cohorts and two completed cooperative group trials, with central pathology review and a minimum of 90 days of follow-up. Staining is scored by two pathologists blinded to outcome, with a third adjudicating discordance above ten percentage points; scores are additionally captured by digital image analysis. Sequencing uses a validated 468-gene panel with a mutational burden calculation restricted to nonsynonymous coding variants after germline and clonal hematopoiesis filtering. Missing data are handled by multiple imputation with sensitivity analyses. With 1400 patients and an anticipated 28 percent response rate we have 90 percent power to detect an odds ratio of 1.9 per standard deviation for each measure in a model containing all three, and 80 percent power for a two-way interaction of that magnitude.

title: Mechanisms and Mitigation of Toxicity Arising from Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Combined nivolumab and ipilimumab produces grade 3 or higher toxicity in roughly 55 percent of treated patients, most commonly colitis, hepatitis, hypophysitis, thyroiditis and inflammatory arthritis. The prevailing assumption is that these events and antitumor activity are mechanistically inseparable, but the evidence is thin and largely correlative. We propose that a defined subset of toxicity is driven by expansion of T cell clones that recognize antigens shared between tumor and affected tissue, while another subset reflects unmasking of pre-existing autoreactive clones and cytokine-driven bystander inflammation, and that these subsets differ in their coupling to tumor control. We will use paired tumor and affected-tissue sampling with receptor sequencing, longitudinal cytokine and autoantibody profiling, and a treatment-decision cohort to test whether targeted cytokine blockade can uncouple toxicity from efficacy.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Determine clonal relationships between tumor-infiltrating and tissue-infiltrating lymphocytes. Paired biopsies from 120 patients with grade 2 or higher colitis, hepatitis or dermatitis will undergo deep TCR beta sequencing alongside the pretreatment tumor to quantify shared clone frequency. Aim 2. Identify pretreatment predictors. Baseline serum autoantibody arrays, IL-6 and CXCL9 levels, thyroid function, and stool 16S rRNA amplicon profiles from 400 patients will be tested against prospectively adjudicated toxicity using penalized regression with nested cross-validation. Aim 3. Test uncoupling strategies. In a randomized phase II design (NCT03934333) patients developing grade 2 colitis will receive tocilizumab or standard high-dose corticosteroids, with co-primary endpoints of symptom resolution at 14 days and best overall tumor response, and with serial receptor sequencing to determine whether tumor-reactive clones are preserved.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Immune-related adverse events are the dominant reason for permanent discontinuation of combination checkpoint therapy, and the reflexive use of high-dose corticosteroids may blunt the antitumor response that motivated treatment. Because clinicians currently have no way to distinguish the patient whose colitis is driven by the same clones that are controlling the tumor from the patient whose colitis is bystander inflammation, management is uniform and maximally immunosuppressive. Establishing that a substantial fraction of events are clonally unrelated to tumor control would justify targeted cytokine blockade as first-line management and could preserve efficacy in thousands of patients annually. The proposal also addresses a persistent equity problem, since patients with pre-existing autoimmune disease are excluded from nearly all registration trials and have no evidence base.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Existing studies profile either the tumor or the inflamed tissue but rarely both from the same patient at the same time point, which makes clonal attribution impossible. Our paired design, with a prespecified shared-clone metric and a permutation-based null accounting for repertoire size, provides the first quantitative test of the shared-antigen hypothesis. The randomized management aim is also unusual: it embeds a mechanistic sampling schedule inside a pragmatic treatment decision, so that the biology and the clinical question are answered in the same patients. Finally, we deliberately enroll patients with controlled pre-existing autoimmune conditions under a protocol-specified monitoring plan, generating the first prospective safety data in a population that represents perhaps one in eight candidates for therapy.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Accrual occurs at five sites over five years. Endoscopic and skin biopsies are obtained within 72 hours of event onset and before immunosuppression whenever feasible; a prespecified sensitivity analysis excludes patients who received steroids first. Receptor sequencing targets 500000 templates per sample with a spike-in synthetic control for clonality normalization. Shared-clone frequency is compared against a permuted null and against unaffected tissue from the same patient. The randomized aim targets 90 patients, giving 85 percent power to exclude a 15 percentage point decrement in response rate under a noninferiority margin, with a prespecified futility interim after 40 patients. All toxicity adjudication uses CTCAE version 5 by a blinded committee.

title: Preoperative Checkpoint Blockade in Resectable Disease: Immune Dynamics and Residual Viable Tumor

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Administering checkpoint blockade before surgery exposes the drug to an intact primary tumor and to its draining lymph nodes, and provides a resection specimen in which the extent of residual viable tumor can be measured directly. Across melanoma and non-small cell lung cancer, patients with ten percent or less residual viable tumor in the resected specimen have markedly prolonged recurrence-free survival, but the immunological correlates of that outcome and the optimal regimen remain undefined. We propose a coordinated program combining two investigator-initiated preoperative trials with an intensive correlative platform. We will define the kinetics of intratumoral clonal expansion during the three to six weeks between first dose and surgery, determine whether plasma tumor-derived DNA clearance anticipates the pathology result, and compare single-agent PD-1 blockade with combined PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade at attenuated doses.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Characterize early intratumoral immune dynamics. Serial fine-needle aspirates at day 0, day 10 and at surgery from 140 patients will be profiled by single-cell RNA and paired receptor sequencing to identify clones that expand within the tumor and to determine whether expansion originates from cells already present at baseline. Aim 2. Establish plasma DNA clearance as an early surrogate. Plasma will be collected at four time points and assayed with a patient-specific multiplex PCR panel; we will estimate the sensitivity and specificity of clearance by day 21 for predicting ten percent or less residual viable tumor. Aim 3. Compare regimens. In a randomized phase II (NCT04205552), 180 patients receive pembrolizumab alone or nivolumab 3 mg/kg with ipilimumab 1 mg/kg for two cycles before resection, with residual viable tumor as the primary endpoint and grade 3 or higher toxicity and surgical delay as co-secondary endpoints.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Adjuvant therapy after resection treats a population in which most patients are already cured and cannot generate a tissue readout, so trials require thousands of patients and years of follow-up. Preoperative treatment inverts that arithmetic. A pathology endpoint available six weeks after enrollment converts regimen selection from a decade-long question into an eighteen-month one, provided the endpoint is validated against survival and the correlative science explains why some patients clear their tumors. Determining whether responding clones are recruited from the periphery or expanded in situ has direct design consequences, since the former would favor systemic priming strategies and the latter would favor intratumoral or nodal delivery. The dosing comparison addresses the central clinical tension between depth of response and toxicity.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Three elements are distinctive. First, serial fine-needle aspiration rather than core biopsy permits sampling at three time points without compromising the resection specimen, and we have validated that a 50-microliter aspirate yields sufficient cells for single-cell chemistry. Second, plasma assay design is patient-specific rather than panel-based, lowering the limit of detection to roughly 0.005 percent variant allele fraction and making day-21 clearance interpretable in early-stage disease where tumor DNA shedding is low. Third, the randomized aim uses an attenuated CTLA-4 dose selected from prior preoperative experience rather than the metastatic-setting dose, testing the hypothesis that in the presence of an intact tumor and its draining nodes a lower dose achieves comparable depth with substantially less toxicity.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Patients with resectable stage IIIB melanoma or stage IB to IIIA lung cancer are eligible. Pathology is assessed centrally by two pathologists using published residual viable tumor criteria with blinded adjudication. Single-cell libraries target 4000 cells per aspirate; clonal expansion is defined as a fivefold increase in a clone occupying at least 0.5 percent of the repertoire, and origin is inferred by comparing to baseline tumor and to matched peripheral blood. The randomized comparison targets 90 patients per arm, giving 80 percent power to detect an increase in the rate of ten percent or less residual viable tumor from 30 to 50 percent at two-sided alpha 0.05. Surgery must occur within six weeks of the first dose and delay beyond that window is a prespecified safety event.

title: The Self-Renewing CD8 Compartment as the Cellular Substrate of PD-1 Blockade

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: PD-1 blockade does not rescue terminally differentiated cytotoxic lymphocytes; it acts on a minority population that retains TCF7 expression, low granzyme content, and the capacity to divide and give rise to effector progeny. We propose that the size and anatomical location of this self-renewing compartment, rather than total lymphocyte density, determines the magnitude and durability of clinical benefit. We will quantify the compartment in serial human specimens using flow cytometry and single-cell transcriptomics with paired receptor capture, define the niche in which it resides using multiplexed imaging, and test in mouse models whether transcriptional enforcement of the progenitor program by TOX modulation or IL-15 support expands the compartment and enlarges the response to anti-PD-1. The work reframes response prediction around a specific cell state rather than around aggregate infiltration.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Quantify the self-renewing compartment and its relationship to outcome. Fresh tumor from 200 patients treated with pembrolizumab or nivolumab will be analyzed by spectral flow cytometry for TCF7, SLAMF6, CD39, TIM-3 and PD-1, and the fraction of tumor-reactive clones residing in the TCF7-positive gate will be determined by paired receptor sequencing. Aim 2. Define the tissue niche. Multiplexed imaging with neighborhood analysis will test the hypothesis that TCF7-positive cells are concentrated in peritumoral CD20-rich aggregates containing CD21-positive stromal networks rather than dispersed within tumor nests. Aim 3. Manipulate the compartment. In B16-F10, MC38 and a genetically engineered melanoma model we will test conditional Tox deletion, IL-15 superagonist support, and 4-1BB agonism for their capacity to expand the progenitor pool and to convert partial responses into durable rejections.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Predictive models built on total cytotoxic lymphocyte density plateau at modest discrimination because they count cells that are already incapable of proliferative response. If benefit is contributed almost entirely by a compartment that constitutes two to eight percent of infiltrating lymphocytes, then assays that ignore differentiation state are measuring mostly noise. Reframing the readout has three consequences: it explains why heavily infiltrated tumors sometimes fail, it identifies a rational target for combination design, and it provides a pharmacodynamic endpoint for early-phase trials that is more proximal than radiographic response. Understanding where these cells reside is equally important, because niche dependence implies that stromal disruption or lymphotoxin blockade could abolish benefit even when the cells themselves are present.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: We integrate three readouts that are usually pursued separately: differentiation state by protein, clonal identity by receptor sequence, and spatial position by imaging, all from the same specimen. This permits the specific test of whether the tumor-reactive clones that expand after therapy were resident in the progenitor gate before treatment. Second, we use conditional rather than germline Tox deletion, timed after tumor establishment, which separates the requirement for the factor in compartment formation from its role in maintenance. Third, our niche hypothesis is testable pharmacologically through lymphotoxin beta receptor blockade, offering a loss-of-function counterpart to the correlative imaging. The panels, gating definitions and imaging pipelines will be released to permit direct replication.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Fresh specimens are collected under an existing tissue protocol with a target of 200 evaluable cases over four years and mandatory processing within four hours. Spectral flow uses a 28-color panel with standardized bead normalization across runs. Single-cell libraries target 5000 cells with 5-prime chemistry and paired alpha and beta chain capture. Association with response uses logistic regression adjusted for prior therapy and disease site; with 200 patients and 32 percent response we have 85 percent power to detect an odds ratio of 2.2 per doubling of compartment fraction. Imaging uses a 24-marker panel with cell-type calling validated against flow on split specimens, and neighborhood enrichment is tested against a permuted spatial null with false discovery rate control.

title: HLA Loss of Heterozygosity and Neoantigen Editing under Immune Selection

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Tumors evolving under lymphocyte pressure can delete one parental HLA haplotype, narrowing the set of peptides they are able to display without abolishing display altogether. We propose that this allele-specific loss is a common and underappreciated route to therapeutic failure, distinct from complete B2M inactivation, and that it produces a characteristic signature: retention of a high nonsynonymous variant count together with selective depletion of peptides predicted to bind the lost allele. We will quantify allele-specific loss in 600 tumors with matched normal sequencing, develop and validate a statistical test for peptide depletion that accounts for trinucleotide context and expression, determine whether loss is enriched at progression relative to baseline, and test in humanized models whether a bispecific engager that bypasses classical presentation retains activity against haplotype-deleted tumors.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Measure allele-specific HLA loss at scale. Using a read-backed haplotype-aware caller on 600 tumor-normal pairs across lung, head and neck and melanoma, we will estimate loss prevalence, its clonality, and its co-occurrence with B2M and TAP1 alterations. Aim 2. Test for peptide depletion under selection. We will compare the observed to expected ratio of predicted binders for retained versus lost alleles, using a context-matched mutational model, and ask whether depletion is stronger in tumors with high cytotoxic infiltration. Aim 3. Determine clinical impact and therapeutic bypass. In 260 patients treated with PD-1 blockade we will test whether loss predicts inferior progression-free survival independent of variant count and ligand expression, and in HLA-humanized mice we will compare a CD3-engaging bispecific against a T cell receptor mimic for activity in haplotype-deleted xenografts.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Selection algorithms that count nonsynonymous variants implicitly assume that all such variants are equally visible. Allele-specific loss breaks that assumption in a way that is invisible to standard panels, which is why the phenomenon has been detected mainly in specialized research cohorts. If a fifth of lung tumors carry clonal haplotype loss, then a fifth of patients selected on variant count alone are being offered a therapy whose mechanism has been partly disabled before the first dose. A validated, panel-compatible detection method would allow this group to be identified prospectively and directed toward modalities that do not require classical peptide display. The peptide-depletion test also provides a general readout of historical immune pressure that is applicable to any sequenced tumor.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: The technical innovation is a haplotype-aware caller that uses phased reads across the polymorphic region together with allele-specific coverage, validated against single-cell DNA sequencing in twenty tumors, which resolves a region that standard copy-number pipelines routinely misassign. The statistical innovation is a depletion test that conditions on the trinucleotide mutational process and on transcript abundance, removing two confounders that have generated conflicting reports about whether editing occurs at all. The translational innovation is the direct comparison of two bypass modalities in the same haplotype-deleted models, which converts a descriptive genomic finding into an actionable therapeutic recommendation rather than leaving it as a negative predictive marker.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Sequencing data come from three institutional cohorts with matched germline and from a prospectively accruing lung study. The caller will be benchmarked on in silico mixtures at known purity and on twenty tumors with orthogonal single-cell validation, targeting sensitivity above 0.90 at purity above 0.4. Survival analyses use Cox models with variant count, ligand score and stage as covariates; with 260 treated patients and an assumed 18 percent loss prevalence we have 80 percent power to detect a hazard ratio of 1.7. Humanized mouse work uses NSG-HLA-A2 recipients with autologous lymphocyte reconstitution, six animals per arm, with prespecified growth and survival analyses and blinded tumor measurement.

title: Adenosine Accumulation and Oxygen Deprivation as Metabolic Restraints on Antitumor CD8 Function

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Regions of solid tumors distant from perfused vessels accumulate extracellular ATP catabolites through the sequential action of CD39 and CD73, and signaling through the A2A receptor raises intracellular cyclic AMP in infiltrating lymphocytes, suppressing granule exocytosis and cytokine output. The same regions show stabilized HIF1A protein, elevated lactate, and low interstitial pH. We propose that these metabolic constraints, rather than checkpoint receptor engagement alone, explain why lymphocytes that are present and antigen-experienced remain functionally inert, and that relieving them is required for PD-1 blockade to work in poorly perfused tumors. We will map the spatial coincidence of catabolite generation, oxygen deprivation and lymphocyte dysfunction in human specimens, dissect the cellular sources of CD73 in mouse models, and test whether receptor antagonism or ectoenzyme blockade restores function and synergizes with anti-PD-1.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Map metabolic and functional gradients in human tumors. Using pimonidazole-labeled surgical specimens, mass spectrometry imaging of adenosine and lactate, and multiplexed immunofluorescence, we will test whether lymphocytes within labeled regions show reduced granzyme B and TNF despite equivalent density. Aim 2. Determine cellular sources and requirements. Conditional Nt5e deletion in tumor cells, in stromal fibroblasts and in CD11b-positive cells will identify the dominant source of catabolite generation in MC38 and B16-F10, with adoptive transfer of A2A receptor-deficient OT-I cells establishing the target compartment. Aim 3. Test therapeutic relief. Small-molecule A2A antagonism, anti-CD73 antibody, and vascular normalization by low-dose anti-VEGFR2 will each be combined with anti-PD-1, with intratumoral oxygen electrode measurements and functional readouts as pharmacodynamic endpoints.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Combination trials pairing checkpoint antibodies with metabolic agents have produced inconsistent results, in part because patients are enrolled without regard to whether the targeted constraint is actually operating in their tumor. A spatially resolved demonstration that catabolite accumulation and lymphocyte inertness are colocalized would justify enrichment strategies based on perfusion imaging or ectoenzyme staining rather than on unselected accrual. The cellular-source question is equally consequential for drug design, since a tumor-cell-dominant source favors direct enzymatic inhibition while a stromal or phagocyte-dominant source favors depleting or reprogramming approaches. The project also produces a quantitative, transferable map linking a physiological variable that can be imaged in patients to a cellular phenotype that currently requires tissue.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: We couple mass spectrometry imaging of the relevant metabolites directly to multiplexed protein imaging on serial sections from the same block, so that metabolite concentration and lymphocyte phenotype are measured in registered coordinates rather than in separate cohorts. Conditional deletion across three distinct compartments in the same tumor models is a level of genetic dissection that has not been applied to this axis. We further introduce an intratumoral electrode protocol that permits repeated oxygen measurement in the same animal before and after vascular normalization, converting a cross-sectional inference into a within-subject test. Finally, a candidate enrichment assay based on ectoenzyme staining intensity will be prespecified and locked, so that its performance can be evaluated rather than derived post hoc.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Human specimens come from 90 surgical resections with pimonidazole administered preoperatively under an existing protocol. Registered serial sections are analyzed with cell segmentation and distance-to-label metrics; functional marker intensity is modeled as a function of distance with mixed-effects regression accounting for patient. Mouse experiments use eight to ten animals per arm with prespecified growth models. Pharmacodynamic sampling occurs at 72 hours after the second dose. For the enrichment analysis, staining intensity is dichotomized at a locked threshold derived from the surgical series and applied without modification to the treated cohort. All imaging analysis is performed blinded to treatment assignment, and code and segmentation models will be deposited on publication.

title: Fc Gamma Receptor Engagement and Intratumoral FOXP3 Cell Elimination by Anti-CTLA-4 Antibodies

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Ipilimumab is usually described as a blocking antibody, yet in mouse models its activity requires the activating Fc gamma receptor on tumor-resident macrophages and is accompanied by selective elimination of intratumoral FOXP3-positive CD4 cells, which express the target at severalfold higher density than conventional cells. Whether the same mechanism operates in patients, and whether it can be enhanced without proportionally increasing toxicity, is unresolved. We propose to quantify the effect in serial human biopsies stratified by FCGR3A V158F genotype, to determine the dose and schedule dependence of the effect using an attenuated-dose randomized comparison, and to test in humanized models whether Fc engineering that increases receptor affinity widens the therapeutic index. The work directly informs whether next-generation agents should be optimized for blockade or for cytotoxic elimination.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Quantify intratumoral FOXP3 cell loss in patients and its genetic modifiers. Paired biopsies before and three weeks after the first ipilimumab dose in 150 patients will be analyzed by multiplexed imaging and flow cytometry, with the ratio of CD8 to FOXP3 cells as the primary readout and FCGR3A genotype as the prespecified modifier. Aim 2. Establish dose and schedule dependence. Within a randomized comparison of 1 mg/kg versus 3 mg/kg given with fixed-dose nivolumab (NCT03887429), we will relate serum concentration and receptor occupancy to the tissue effect and to grade 3 or higher toxicity. Aim 3. Test Fc engineering in humanized models. Variants with enhanced receptor affinity, with abolished binding, and with the parental Fc will be compared in FCGR-humanized mice for tissue effect, tumor control, and colonic inflammation.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: The field has spent a decade optimizing checkpoint antibodies for receptor blockade while the animal data point to cell elimination as the dominant mechanism of the CTLA-4 class. If elimination is what matters, then affinity for the ligand-binding pocket is largely irrelevant and the design problem becomes one of engineering effector function and restricting it to the tumor bed. The dose comparison is immediately actionable: attenuated dosing with fixed-dose PD-1 blockade is already used in practice on empirical grounds without any mechanistic evidence that the tissue effect is preserved. Establishing genotype dependence would also provide the first germline predictor of benefit for this class, and one that is inexpensive and available before the first dose.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Human studies of this mechanism have been limited to single-arm series with unmatched timing, which cannot separate drug effect from sampling variation. Our design nests paired mandatory biopsies inside a randomized dose comparison, so the tissue effect is estimated with a within-patient contrast and compared between randomized arms. We add receptor occupancy measured on circulating monocytes as a bridging pharmacodynamic variable, allowing the tissue effect to be related to exposure rather than to nominal dose. In the preclinical aim we use a receptor-humanized strain rather than wild-type mice, because the mouse and human receptor families differ substantially in cell-type distribution and in affinity, a difference that has produced misleading translation in this exact system.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Accrual of 150 patients with advanced melanoma or renal cell carcinoma occurs over four years at four sites; biopsy at week three is mandatory and non-compliance above 15 percent triggers a protocol amendment. Imaging uses a 12-marker panel with automated segmentation and a locked gating definition; the primary analysis is a paired comparison of log CD8 to FOXP3 ratio by Wilcoxon signed rank, with genotype interaction tested in a linear model. The randomized comparison is powered at 80 percent to detect a 0.5 standard deviation difference in the tissue effect between dose arms with 75 evaluable patients per arm. Mouse studies use eight animals per arm; colonic inflammation is scored histologically by a blinded pathologist using a validated five-point index.

title: Commensal Determinants of Checkpoint Blockade Efficacy and Toxicity

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Retrospective series consistently report that patients receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics in the month before starting PD-1 blockade have inferior survival, and that stool composition differs between responders and non-responders, but the reported taxa differ across studies and causal evidence in humans is absent. We propose a program that treats the intestinal community as a modifiable exposure rather than a biomarker. We will assemble a prospective cohort of 500 patients with melanoma or lung cancer with banked stool at three time points and adjudicated antibiotic exposure, transfer defined communities from human donors into germ-free mice bearing syngeneic tumors to test causality, and conduct a randomized trial of a defined bacterial consortium given before and during pembrolizumab. Mechanistic work focuses on how community-derived short-chain fatty acids and secondary bile acids alter intestinal and intratumoral phagocyte programs.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Define exposure-outcome relationships prospectively. In 500 patients we will relate antibiotic class, timing and duration, and shotgun metagenomic composition at baseline, week 6 and week 12, to objective response and to adjudicated grade 2 or higher colitis, using inverse probability weighting for confounding by indication. Aim 2. Establish causality by transfer. Communities from ten responders and ten non-responders will be transferred into germ-free C57BL/6 mice implanted with MC38 or B16-F10, with tumor growth under anti-PD-1 as the endpoint and reciprocal transfers as controls. Aim 3. Test a defined consortium in patients. A randomized phase II (NCT04116775) will assign 120 patients to an eleven-strain consortium or placebo starting two weeks before pembrolizumab, with objective response rate as the primary endpoint and engraftment by metagenomics as a required pharmacodynamic criterion.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: If the intestinal community is causal, it is the only major determinant of checkpoint blockade outcome that can be changed in weeks and at low cost. The clinical stakes are immediate: antibiotics are prescribed to a third of patients around the start of therapy, frequently for indications that would tolerate a narrower agent or watchful waiting, and no guideline currently weighs the oncologic cost of that decision. The question of immune-related adverse events is equally important, since the same communities that support antitumor activity may lower the threshold for colitis, and a consortium that improved response while worsening toxicity would not be a net benefit. Only a design that measures both endpoints prospectively in the same patients can distinguish these possibilities.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Most published work in this area is retrospective, uses 16S profiling that cannot resolve strain or function, and reports taxa selected after the fact from small cohorts, which explains the poor replication across studies. We use shotgun metagenomics with strain-level resolution and prespecify a functional pathway analysis rather than a taxon list. The germ-free transfer aim uses human donors from our own prospectively characterized cohort rather than from published cohorts, so donor phenotype is measured with the same assays as the recipients. The randomized aim requires demonstrated engraftment as an analysis criterion, which prevents the common failure mode in which a negative efficacy result is uninterpretable because the intervention never took hold.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Patients are enrolled before their first dose at four sites; stool is self-collected into stabilizing buffer and antibiotic exposure is abstracted from pharmacy records and adjudicated by two reviewers. Metagenomic sequencing targets 20 million paired reads per sample with strain profiling and pathway abundance quantification. The primary exposure analysis uses inverse probability of treatment weighting with covariates including performance status, corticosteroid use, prior lines, and infection indication. With 500 patients and an expected 30 percent antibiotic exposure we have 82 percent power to detect a hazard ratio of 1.5. The randomized consortium trial targets 60 patients per arm for 80 percent power to detect an increase in response rate from 35 to 55 percent.

title: A Spatially Resolved Atlas of the Tumor Immune Microenvironment across Checkpoint Blockade Outcomes

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Bulk expression profiling averages over cellular neighborhoods that differ by an order of magnitude in composition within a single tumor section, and single-cell dissociation discards the geometry that determines which cells can interact. We propose to build a coordinated resource in which the same tumor blocks are profiled by whole-transcriptome slide-based capture, by 40-plex antibody imaging at subcellular resolution, and by dissociated single-cell sequencing with paired receptor capture, across 260 patients with lung, melanoma, head and neck and renal tumors treated with PD-1 blockade and with known outcomes. The analytic goal is a small set of recurrent cellular neighborhoods with reproducible composition, and a demonstration that neighborhood abundance predicts response better than either cell-type frequency or bulk signatures derived from the same specimens.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Generate matched multimodal data on a common specimen set. For each of 260 tumors we will produce slide-based whole-transcriptome capture at 55-micron resolution, 40-marker antibody imaging on an adjacent section, and dissociated single-cell libraries from a matched fragment, with standardized processing and randomized batch assignment. Aim 2. Define and name recurrent neighborhoods. Using a graph-based neighborhood model with cross-site holdout, we will identify neighborhood types, quantify their reproducibility across platforms and across pathology sites, and provide a projection tool that assigns neighborhoods in new specimens. Aim 3. Test predictive performance against outcome. Neighborhood abundance will be compared with cell-type frequency, ligand immunohistochemistry, and bulk expression signatures for prediction of objective response and progression-free survival, using nested cross-validation and a locked held-out set of 80 specimens.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: The field currently has many partial descriptions of the tumor immune landscape generated on different platforms in different cohorts, which cannot be compared because platform and cohort are confounded. A single specimen set profiled on all three modalities allows the community to answer a question it cannot currently answer: how much of the biology reported by one technology is recoverable from another, and how much predictive information is genuinely spatial rather than compositional. Because the resource is designed as a benchmark, with locked splits and a projection tool, it will support method development for years beyond the funding period. The neighborhood definitions are also directly usable as pharmacodynamic endpoints in early-phase combination trials, where tissue is scarce and assay choice is currently arbitrary.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Existing atlases are single-platform and single-institution. Ours is multimodal on the same block, multi-institutional by design, and explicitly structured for method benchmarking with sequestered evaluation data. We introduce a projection model that assigns neighborhood identity to new specimens without requiring the full panel, lowering the barrier to adoption. We also quantify cross-site reproducibility as a primary rather than incidental result, reporting the fraction of neighborhood variance attributable to site, batch and pathology handling. Finally, all raw images, count matrices and outcome labels will be released under a data use agreement with a public leaderboard for the held-out prediction task, an arrangement borrowed from machine learning benchmarks and rare in tissue pathology.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Blocks come from four institutional biobanks with linked outcomes and a minimum 24-month follow-up. Slide-based capture and antibody imaging are performed on adjacent 5-micron sections; dissociated libraries come from an adjacent fragment. Batch assignment is randomized with respect to outcome and site, and control tissue is included on every run. Neighborhood models are fit on 180 specimens with fivefold cross-validation and evaluated once on the 80-specimen holdout after the analysis plan is registered. Comparative prediction uses the same folds for all feature sets, with DeLong tests for paired area under the curve and a prespecified superiority margin of 0.05. Variance components by site, batch and operator are estimated with a mixed-effects model.

title: Loss-of-function JAK1 and JAK2 alterations at progression after initial response to pembrolizumab in metastatic melanoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We sequenced 96 paired pre-treatment and progression biopsies from patients with metastatic melanoma who achieved a confirmed partial or complete response to pembrolizumab and subsequently progressed after a median of 19.4 months. Truncating or damaging missense alterations in JAK1 or JAK2 were present in 11 of 96 progression specimens (11.5 percent, 95 percent CI 5.9 to 19.6) and in 2 of 96 matched baseline specimens. In 9 of the 11 cases the alteration was accompanied by loss of the wild-type allele. Progression-derived lines carrying these alterations failed to upregulate surface HLA-A, B and C or to secrete CXCL9 after cytokine exposure, and were resistant to killing by autologous tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes despite retained peptide presentation at baseline. Duplex sequencing detected the identical variant at a mean allele fraction of 0.9 percent in 4 of 11 matched baseline samples, indicating selection of a pre-existing subclone rather than de novo mutation.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Objective responses to PD-1 blockade in melanoma are durable in most patients but not all: a quarter to a third of responders eventually progress, and the mechanisms are poorly characterized relative to those of primary treatment failure. One candidate is tumor-intrinsic unresponsiveness to the cytokines produced by the very lymphocytes that mediate the initial response. A T cell-inflamed transcriptional signature dominated by CXCL9, CXCL10, STAT1 and HLA-DRA was previously shown to identify tumors likely to respond to PD-1 blockade across multiple histologies, with an area under the curve of 0.73 in an independent validation cohort, which places the intact cytokine-response module upstream of clinical benefit. Separately, allele-specific loss of class I haplotypes has been reported to constrain the diversity of displayed peptides in lung tumors under lymphocyte pressure. Here we ask whether the signaling module itself is inactivated at the time of late progression.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients treated at two centers under NCT03521739 underwent biopsy at baseline and at radiographic progression. Whole-exome sequencing was performed on tumor and matched germline DNA at a mean target coverage of 190-fold, with a 512-gene duplex-barcoded panel applied to baseline samples for subclone detection at a limit of 0.2 percent allele fraction. Short-term cultures were established from 34 progression biopsies. Surface class I molecules were measured by flow cytometry after 48 hours of exposure to 100 units per milliliter of recombinant cytokine, and chemokine secretion was measured by multiplex bead assay. Autologous killing assays used expanded tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes at effector-to-target ratios of 1:1 to 10:1 with impedance-based readout. Variant calling used a consensus of three callers with manual review; statistical comparisons used exact tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Eleven progression specimens carried damaging JAK1 or JAK2 alterations, including four frameshift, three nonsense and four missense variants at conserved kinase-domain residues. Median variant allele fraction adjusted for purity was 0.71, consistent with clonal or near-clonal representation. Nine specimens showed accompanying copy loss of the second allele. In culture, altered lines showed no increase in surface class I density after cytokine exposure (mean fold change 1.04 versus 3.8 in unaltered lines, p equals 0.0004) and secreted 22-fold less CXCL9. Killing by autologous lymphocytes was reduced from 61 percent to 9 percent specific lysis at a 10:1 ratio. Duplex sequencing of matched baselines detected the identical variant in four cases at 0.4 to 1.6 percent allele fraction. Patients whose progression specimens carried an alteration had shorter post-progression survival (median 7.1 versus 15.9 months, hazard ratio 2.3, p equals 0.01).

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: These data establish that late progression on PD-1 blockade is frequently accompanied by inactivation of the tumor-intrinsic cytokine response module, and that in a substantial minority of cases the responsible clone was detectable before treatment at very low abundance. The observation that a T cell-inflamed signature enriched for CXCL9 and STAT1 predicts initial benefit is complementary to ours: the same module that must be intact to permit a response is what is subsequently lost. Practically, our findings argue that rebiopsy at progression should include an assessment of pathway integrity, because patients whose tumors can no longer respond to lymphocyte-derived cytokines are unlikely to benefit from agents that act by increasing effector output. Limitations include the modest number of altered cases, the restriction to melanoma, and the possibility that culture selects for subpopulations not dominant in vivo.

title: Biallelic B2M inactivation and class I surface loss define a subset of PD-1-refractory non-small cell lung cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Among 412 patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer treated with first-line pembrolizumab, 38 (9.2 percent) had tumors with biallelic B2M inactivation by combined mutation and copy-number analysis. These tumors showed absent surface beta-2-microglobulin by immunohistochemistry in 34 of 38 cases and had an objective response rate of 2.6 percent compared with 31.8 percent in the B2M-intact group (p less than 0.001), despite equivalent PD-L1 tumor proportion scores and equivalent nonsynonymous variant counts (median 9.4 versus 8.8 per megabase). Median progression-free survival was 2.1 months versus 8.4 months (hazard ratio 3.1, 95 percent CI 2.1 to 4.6). In 30 of 38 cases the alteration was clonal in the pre-treatment specimen, indicating that the defect preceded therapy rather than emerging under selection. NK cell infiltration was higher in inactivated tumors but was not associated with response.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Patient selection for first-line PD-1 blockade in lung cancer relies on ligand immunohistochemistry and, increasingly, on variant counts, both of which describe the input to recognition rather than the capacity of the tumor to be recognized. The light chain of the class I complex is obligatory for surface assembly, and its loss abolishes display of every peptide regardless of how many are generated. Prior work in melanoma showed that inactivation of the tumor cytokine response module can be selected at late progression from subclones detectable before treatment at fractions below two percent, which raises the question of whether display defects in lung cancer follow the same acquired trajectory or are instead present from the outset. We therefore examined a large consecutive series treated uniformly in the first-line setting.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Consecutive patients receiving first-line pembrolizumab with or without platinum doublet at four institutions between 2016 and 2020 were identified from a prospectively maintained registry with independent radiology review. Tumor and matched normal sequencing used a 468-gene panel with allele-specific copy number and purity estimation; biallelic inactivation required a damaging variant with loss of the second allele or homozygous deletion. Immunohistochemistry for beta-2-microglobulin and for PD-L1 with the 22C3 clone was performed on the same block. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on 22 fresh specimens. Response was assessed by RECIST 1.1. Survival was analyzed with Cox models adjusted for performance status, ligand score, smoking history and treatment regimen; the primary comparison was prespecified.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Biallelic events comprised 21 truncating variants with loss of heterozygosity, 11 homozygous deletions and 6 splice-site alterations. Surface light chain staining was absent or minimal in 34 of 38. Response rates were 2.6 percent versus 31.8 percent, and the difference persisted in the subgroup with tumor proportion score of 50 percent or higher (5.0 percent versus 44.1 percent). Variant counts did not differ between groups, and a signature score for the cytokine response module was preserved, indicating that the defect was downstream of signaling rather than a failure to sense. Single-cell analysis showed comparable CD8 infiltration but a threefold reduction in the fraction of CD8 cells expressing granzyme B. Among 14 patients rebiopsied at progression, no new B2M events were detected in the intact group.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: In lung cancer, loss of the obligate class I light chain is a pre-existing rather than a treatment-acquired lesion, which distinguishes it from the pattern reported for kinase-module inactivation at late progression in melanoma, where the responsible clone was present before treatment at allele fractions near one percent and was selected over roughly 19 months of therapy. The practical implication is that light chain staining, which costs a fraction of a sequencing assay, identifies a group of patients for whom ligand-directed selection is actively misleading, since a third of them meet the high-expression threshold that would otherwise direct them to single-agent therapy. The higher NK infiltration we observed did not translate into benefit, tempering enthusiasm for the notion that display-null tumors are automatically susceptible to innate effectors.

title: A T cell-inflamed transcriptional signature predicts response to PD-1 blockade across nine tumor types

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We derived an 18-gene expression signature dominated by CXCL9, CXCL10, STAT1, IDO1, HLA-DRA, CD8A and GZMK from pre-treatment tumors of 220 patients receiving pembrolizumab or nivolumab, and validated it in an independent set of 314 patients spanning nine histologies. Signature-high tumors had an objective response rate of 42 percent versus 11 percent in signature-low tumors, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.73 (95 percent CI 0.67 to 0.79) in validation. The signature was only modestly correlated with nonsynonymous variant count (Spearman rho 0.21) and with ligand immunohistochemistry (rho 0.38), and a model combining all three improved discrimination to 0.78. In tumors with high signature scores that nevertheless failed to respond, a myeloid module marked by SPP1, TREM2 and MARCO was enriched 2.4-fold, suggesting a distinct mode of failure downstream of lymphocyte recruitment.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Two broad explanations exist for failure of PD-1 blockade. In one, lymphocytes never reach the tumor because the tumor generates no chemotactic signal and displays little antigenic material. In the other, lymphocytes arrive but are restrained by the local environment. Distinguishing these possibilities before treatment would allow rational assignment to different combination strategies, but the assays in routine use, ligand immunohistochemistry and variant counting, do not address either question directly. Assays of mismatch repair status identify a group with exceptional benefit but describe only a small minority of patients outside colorectal and endometrial primaries. We therefore sought a transcriptional readout of the adaptive signal actually present in the tumor at baseline, derived and validated across histologies rather than within a single disease.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Pre-treatment formalin-fixed specimens from 534 patients were profiled on a 770-gene hybridization panel with housekeeping normalization. The derivation cohort of 220 patients was used for feature selection by elastic-net logistic regression with tenfold cross-validation; the resulting 18-gene score was locked before the validation set was unblinded. Ligand immunohistochemistry used the 22C3 clone with tumor proportion scoring by two pathologists. Sequencing on a 468-gene panel provided variant counts after germline filtering. Response was RECIST 1.1 by blinded central review. Discrimination was compared by DeLong test; calibration was assessed by the Hosmer-Lemeshow statistic. The myeloid module analysis was prespecified for signature-high non-responders and used gene set variation analysis with permutation-based significance.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: The locked score separated responders from non-responders in validation with an area under the curve of 0.73 and retained significance after adjustment for histology, line of therapy and variant count (odds ratio 2.6 per standard deviation, p less than 0.001). Performance was consistent across histologies except renal cell carcinoma, where discrimination fell to 0.58. Combining the score with variant count and ligand score raised the area under the curve to 0.78 (DeLong p equals 0.03 versus signature alone). Among 61 signature-high non-responders, the SPP1 and TREM2 module was enriched relative to signature-high responders (normalized enrichment score 2.1, false discovery rate 0.004), and these tumors also showed higher expression of NT5E and VEGFA. Median progression-free survival was 9.2 months in signature-high versus 2.8 months in signature-low patients.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: A transcriptional readout of the adaptive signal present before treatment carries information that is largely independent of the two assays in routine clinical use, and the combination outperforms any single measure. The failure of the signature in renal cell carcinoma is notable and consistent with the long-standing observation that infiltration in that disease is not organized around the same axis. The enrichment of a lipid-handling and osteopontin-expressing phagocyte module among signature-high non-responders points to a second, downstream barrier, and identifies the patients in whom a combination targeting that compartment would be expected to add value. We caution that the signature is measured on a single archival block and that intratumoral heterogeneity in chemokine expression is substantial.

title: Depleting antibody against TREM2 removes lipid-handling macrophages and restores sensitivity to PD-1 blockade in refractory syngeneic tumors

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We generated a depleting monoclonal antibody against mouse TREM2 and evaluated it in MC38, B16-F10 and LLC tumors that are minimally responsive to anti-PD-1. Treatment reduced the abundance of Trem2-high, Apoe-high, Spp1-high macrophages by 78 percent within 96 hours without altering monocyte or dendritic cell numbers. Single-agent activity was modest (mean tumor growth inhibition 24 percent), but the combination with anti-PD-1 produced complete rejection in 9 of 12 MC38-bearing mice versus 1 of 12 with anti-PD-1 alone (p equals 0.003), and rejected animals resisted rechallenge at 90 days. Depletion increased the fraction of intratumoral CD8 cells co-producing TNF and IFN-gamma from 8 to 31 percent and increased granzyme B release threefold. An Fc-silent variant of the same clone had no effect, establishing that removal of the cell rather than blockade of the receptor is required.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Tumors that contain abundant lymphocytes yet do not respond to checkpoint blockade present a distinct therapeutic problem from those that are immunologically empty. A conserved macrophage state defined by TREM2, APOE, SPP1 and C1QC has been described across human tumor types and was reported to be enriched in patients whose tumors failed PD-1 blockade despite an intact adaptive signal at baseline. Whether that state is a marker of failure or a cause has not been established, because prior interventions relied on germline deletion, which alters myelopoiesis from birth, or on blocking antibodies whose effect on cell survival was not measured. A single-cell survey of human and mouse tumors previously showed that this state occupies the terminal branch of a differentiation trajectory beginning with recruited monocytes, and predicted that its removal would be tolerated.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: A rat anti-mouse TREM2 IgG2a and an LALA-PG Fc-silent variant of the same clone were produced and characterized for binding affinity by surface plasmon resonance. C57BL/6 mice bearing established MC38, B16-F10 or LLC tumors of 80 to 120 cubic millimeters received 200 micrograms twice weekly with or without 200 micrograms anti-PD-1, twelve animals per arm. Tumors were harvested at 96 hours and at endpoint for single-cell RNA sequencing, spectral flow cytometry and multiplexed imaging. Functional assays measured cytokine co-production after brief ex vivo restimulation and granzyme B release by ELISPOT. Growth curves were analyzed with mixed-effects models and survival with log-rank tests; investigators measuring tumors were blinded to treatment assignment.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Depletion was selective: the Trem2-high cluster fell from 31 to 7 percent of CD45-positive cells while Ly6C-high monocytes and cDC1 numbers were unchanged. Combination therapy produced complete rejection in 9 of 12 MC38 and 5 of 12 B16-F10 animals, compared with 1 of 12 and 0 of 12 with anti-PD-1 alone. Median survival was not reached versus 28 days. Intratumoral CD8 cells from combination-treated animals showed increased polyfunctional cytokine co-production, reduced surface TIM-3 and LAG-3, and a 2.7-fold expansion of the TCF7-positive subset. Multiplexed imaging showed redistribution of CD8 cells from the invasive margin into tumor nests, with mean distance to the nearest tumor cell falling from 62 to 21 micrometers. The Fc-silent variant depleted no cells and conferred no benefit despite equivalent receptor occupancy.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: These results convert a correlative association into a causal claim: the lipid-handling macrophage state actively enforces failure of PD-1 blockade, and its physical removal is sufficient to restore sensitivity in three refractory models. The requirement for an intact Fc, demonstrated by the inactive silent variant, indicates that clinical translation should prioritize depleting formats over signaling antagonists, a distinction that several ongoing programs have not made. Our findings are consistent with the single-cell trajectory analysis that placed this state at the terminus of a monocyte-derived differentiation path and predicted that mature cells rather than their precursors carry the suppressive activity. Limitations include the absence of an orthotopic model, the short observation window for autoimmune toxicity, and uncertainty about whether the human receptor supports equivalent depletion given differences in effector cell distribution.

title: Single-cell and spatial profiling identifies conserved SPP1 and TREM2 macrophage states associated with checkpoint blockade failure

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We profiled 184 tumors from patients with melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer and renal cell carcinoma before and during PD-1 blockade, generating 1.14 million single-cell transcriptomes with paired receptor capture and matched slide-based spatial capture on 62 specimens. Mononuclear phagocytes resolved into nine reproducible states, of which two, an SPP1-high state and a TREM2-high APOE-high lipid-handling state, were enriched in patients without objective response (odds ratio 2.9 and 3.4 per interquartile increase, both false discovery rate below 0.01). Trajectory analysis placed both states at the terminus of a path beginning with recruited CD14-positive monocytes. Spatially, TREM2-high cells formed a contiguous band at the invasive margin, and the density of that band was inversely correlated with the depth of CD8 penetration into tumor nests (Spearman rho minus 0.61). On-treatment expansion of the SPP1-high state preceded radiographic progression by a median of 6.8 weeks.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: The mononuclear phagocyte compartment of human tumors has resisted stable classification because dissociation protocols, tissue handling and clustering choices all shift the apparent composition. Consequently, reports linking macrophage phenotype to immunotherapy outcome have been difficult to compare across studies. A separate line of evidence from bulk profiling had shown that tumors with a strong baseline adaptive signal but no clinical benefit are enriched for transcripts including SPP1, TREM2 and MARCO, which suggested a second barrier acting downstream of lymphocyte recruitment but could not identify the responsible cells. We set out to resolve that compartment at single-cell resolution with harmonized processing across three diseases and to determine where the implicated cells sit relative to tumor and lymphocyte compartments.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Fresh specimens were processed within three hours using a cold dissociation protocol to limit stress signatures. Libraries used 5-prime chemistry with paired alpha and beta chain capture, targeting 6000 cells per sample. State assignment used reference projection with bootstrap confidence intervals and was validated by multiplexed immunofluorescence on adjacent sections. Slide-based whole-transcriptome capture at 55-micron resolution was performed on 62 blocks with deconvolution against the matched single-cell reference. Association with best overall response used mixed-effects logistic regression with disease as a random effect and adjustment for prior therapy and line. Spatial analyses used distance-to-margin metrics with permutation nulls. All analyses were prespecified except the trajectory reconstruction, which is labeled exploratory.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Nine phagocyte states were recovered in all three diseases with concordant marker sets. The TREM2-high APOE-high state constituted a median of 18 percent of phagocytes in non-responders versus 7 percent in responders, and the SPP1-high state 22 versus 9 percent. Both associations survived adjustment. Lymphocytes in TREM2-high tumors showed reduced granzyme B and reduced TNF co-production despite equivalent density, and clonal expansion after therapy was one-third as frequent. In spatial data, TREM2-high cells were concentrated within 80 micrometers of the tumor-stroma interface, forming a band whose density predicted shallow CD8 penetration. TREM2-high cells were also concentrated in regions with elevated HIF1A target gene expression and reduced vascular density. In 41 patients with on-treatment sampling, expansion of the SPP1-high state at week 6 preceded radiographic progression in 29, with a positive predictive value of 0.71.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Harmonized processing across three diseases yields a phagocyte taxonomy that reproduces where earlier studies conflicted, and identifies two states whose abundance tracks with treatment failure independent of lymphocyte density. The bulk-profiling observation that tumors with a strong baseline chemokine and interferon-response signature can still fail, and that such tumors over-express SPP1 and TREM2, is explained here by a specific cell population occupying a specific location. The spatial finding is mechanistically suggestive rather than conclusive, since a band of cells at the margin could exclude lymphocytes or could accumulate where lymphocytes have already stalled. Interventional data are needed, and the on-treatment kinetics we report suggest that phagocyte state abundance may serve as an early pharmacodynamic endpoint for such trials.

title: Intratumoral B cells and organized lymphoid aggregates predict benefit from checkpoint blockade in melanoma and soft tissue sarcoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We examined 268 pre-treatment specimens from patients with metastatic melanoma or soft tissue sarcoma receiving PD-1 blockade with or without CTLA-4 blockade.
