Aggregates containing CD20-positive B cell zones adjacent to CD3-positive zones, with CD21-positive follicular dendritic networks and PNAd-positive high endothelial venules, were present in 96 specimens. Objective response was 51 percent in aggregate-positive versus 18 percent in aggregate-negative tumors (p less than 0.001), and the association was independent of CD8 density and of PD-L1 tumor proportion score in multivariable analysis (adjusted odds ratio 3.2, 95 percent CI 1.8 to 5.7). B cell density alone outperformed CD8 density for prediction (area under the curve 0.71 versus 0.62). In sarcoma, where the overall response rate was 16 percent, aggregate-positive tumors responded at 44 percent. Aggregate-positive tumors were enriched for immunoglobulin transcripts with evidence of somatic hypermutation.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Predictive biomarkers for checkpoint blockade have concentrated on tumor cell properties and on the density of cytotoxic lymphocytes, yet both perform inconsistently and neither captures whether the tumor bed can sustain a local immune reaction. Organized lymphoid aggregates containing B cell follicles have been described in many solid tumors and are associated with favorable prognosis in untreated disease, but their relationship to therapeutic response has not been tested in diseases where the response rate is low enough for a strong predictor to be clinically decisive. A separate literature has shown that the lymphocytes capable of responding to PD-1 blockade are a minority subset retaining TCF7 expression and self-renewal capacity, and that these cells occupy defined niches rather than being dispersed. Sarcoma provides a stringent test setting.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Archival blocks from three completed trials and two registries were stained with a seven-marker multiplex panel (CD3, CD8, CD20, CD21, PNAd, PD-L1, pan-cytokeratin) and scanned at 20-fold magnification. Aggregates were called by two pathologists blinded to outcome, with a third adjudicating disagreements; 60 slides were double-read to estimate reliability. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed on 154 specimens with immunoglobulin repertoire reconstruction from unselected reads. Response was RECIST 1.1 by investigator assessment with central confirmation in the trial cases. Logistic regression models included CD8 density, ligand score, disease, line of therapy and regimen. Survival analyses used Cox models stratified by disease. Reliability was summarized by Fleiss kappa.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Aggregates were present in 96 of 268 specimens (36 percent), with substantial interobserver reliability (Fleiss kappa 0.74). Response rates were 51 versus 18 percent overall, 58 versus 26 percent in melanoma, and 44 versus 9 percent in sarcoma. The adjusted odds ratio for aggregate presence was 3.2 and remained significant after adding a 12-gene cytotoxicity score. Median progression-free survival was 14.7 versus 3.1 months (hazard ratio 0.42). Immunoglobulin heavy chain repertoires from aggregate-positive tumors showed higher clonality (mean Gini 0.38 versus 0.19) and a higher mutation rate in the variable region (4.9 versus 1.6 percent), consistent with local affinity maturation. Aggregate-positive tumors also contained a 3.1-fold higher fraction of CD8 cells lacking terminal differentiation markers, concentrated within 100 micrometers of the B cell zone.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: The presence of organized lymphoid aggregates with evidence of germinal center activity identifies patients likely to benefit from checkpoint blockade, and does so with information not contained in cytotoxic lymphocyte density or ligand expression. The magnitude of the effect in sarcoma is clinically important because it converts a disease with a 16 percent response rate into two groups with very different expected benefit. Our observation that less differentiated CD8 cells cluster near the B cell zone is consistent with the proposal that the response to PD-1 blockade is contributed by a self-renewing subset which requires a supportive niche, and suggests that the aggregate is that niche. The main limitation is that aggregate calling on standard sections remains partly subjective despite acceptable reliability, and prospective validation with a locked grading rule is needed.

title: Maturation grade of tertiary lymphoid structures, not their presence, determines survival after PD-1 blockade in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We applied a four-marker maturation grade to tertiary lymphoid structures in 312 pre-treatment specimens from patients with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma treated with pembrolizumab or nivolumab. Structures were graded as early, primary follicle-like, or germinal center containing on the basis of CD21, CD23, Ki-67 and AICDA staining. Structures of any grade were present in 148 specimens (47 percent), but only germinal center containing structures were associated with outcome: median overall survival was 24.6 months for that group versus 9.8 months for early structures and 8.9 months for structure-negative tumors (log-rank p less than 0.001), with no difference between the latter two. Grade remained significant after adjustment for PD-L1 combined positive score, HPV status and performance status (hazard ratio 0.47). Interobserver reliability across six pathologists was acceptable (Fleiss kappa 0.72).

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Reports on the prognostic value of tertiary lymphoid structures in treated cancer are inconsistent, with effect sizes ranging from strongly protective to null across otherwise similar cohorts. One plausible explanation is that the binary present-or-absent scoring used in most studies aggregates biologically distinct entities: loose perivascular lymphocyte collections and fully organized follicles with active germinal centers are both scored positive on hematoxylin and eosin sections. Earlier work in melanoma and sarcoma reported that aggregate-positive tumors responded at 51 percent versus 18 percent and that the effect was independent of cytotoxic lymphocyte density, but scoring in that study was also binary, leaving open whether the signal was carried by all structures or only by the mature ones. Head and neck cancer, with intermediate structure prevalence, permits a direct test.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Specimens were drawn from two institutional registries and one completed trial, with a median follow-up of 41 months. A seven-marker multiplex immunofluorescence panel was applied in a single batch with tissue microarray controls on every slide. Grading followed a prespecified rule: germinal center containing required at least one CD21-positive network with more than 20 percent Ki-67-positive B cells and detectable AICDA. Six pathologists graded a 70-slide subset for reliability. Digital spatial profiling of 48 regions of interest was performed on 40 specimens to compare transcriptional programs by grade. Survival was analyzed with Cox models; the primary comparison of germinal center containing versus all other specimens was prespecified, and grade was also modeled as an ordinal variable.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Grade distribution was 61 early, 42 primary follicle-like and 45 germinal center containing. Only the highest grade was associated with survival, and the ordinal model showed a clear threshold rather than a gradient. Median overall survival was 24.6 versus 9.8 versus 8.9 months across the three groups, and objective response rates were 39, 17 and 15 percent. Regional transcriptional profiling showed that germinal center containing structures were enriched for AICDA, BCL6, CXCL13 and LTB, and that adjacent tumor regions had higher CXCL9 and lower NT5E. Structure grade was only weakly correlated with combined positive score (Spearman rho 0.19). Among 84 patients with archival specimens from both the primary and a metastatic site, grade was concordant in 61 (73 percent).

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Grading resolves a literature inconsistency: the survival signal attributed to tertiary lymphoid structures is carried entirely by the subset with active germinal centers, and studies whose cohorts happened to be dominated by immature structures would report null results. Our findings refine the earlier melanoma and sarcoma analysis that established a response difference of 51 versus 18 percent using binary scoring, by showing that binary scoring dilutes rather than reverses the effect. Practically, the grading rule requires only two additional markers beyond a standard panel and achieved acceptable agreement across six readers, which makes it deployable. Limitations include retrospective design, the modest number of paired primary and metastatic specimens, and the possibility that grade at a single site does not represent the patient overall.

title: Independent and joint predictive value of PD-L1 tumor proportion score and tumor mutational burden in 946 patients receiving PD-1 blockade

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We centrally generated PD-L1 immunohistochemistry with the 22C3 clone and 468-gene panel sequencing on archival blocks from 946 patients with non-small cell lung cancer, urothelial carcinoma, melanoma or gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma treated with pembrolizumab, nivolumab or atezolizumab. Tumor proportion score and tumor mutational burden were only weakly correlated (Spearman rho 0.16). Both independently predicted objective response: adjusted odds ratio 2.1 per tenfold increase in score and 1.8 per doubling of burden. Patients high for both measures had a 51 percent response rate compared with 8 percent for patients low for both, and the two discordant groups responded at 24 and 27 percent. A combined model achieved an area under the curve of 0.70 versus 0.63 and 0.62 for the single measures (DeLong p equals 0.008). Decision-curve analysis showed net benefit for the combined rule across threshold probabilities of 0.15 to 0.45.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Regulatory approvals in this class have been granted on the basis of different companion assays measured in different trials, and clinicians routinely compare results across studies as though the measures were interchangeable. They are not: ligand immunohistochemistry reports an adaptive response of the tissue to local cytokines, while mutational burden reports the quantity of altered protein available for recognition. Prior comparisons have almost always been performed on separate cohorts, or with one assay generated locally and the other centrally, which confounds the biology with tissue handling and scoring practice. Analytical studies have also shown that burden estimates from targeted panels carry appreciable variance at the low end of the range, which further degrades cross-study comparison. We therefore generated both assays centrally from the same block.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Blocks were retrieved for 946 of 1104 eligible patients. Staining was scored by two pathologists blinded to outcome with adjudication of discordances above ten percentage points, and by digital image analysis in parallel. Sequencing used a 468-gene panel with matched normal; burden was computed from nonsynonymous coding variants after germline and clonal hematopoiesis filtering and normalized to the captured coding footprint. Response was RECIST 1.1 with blinded central review in 611 cases and investigator assessment otherwise. Models were fit with logistic and Cox regression including disease, line of therapy, performance status and regimen. The combined rule was fit on a 630-patient training set and evaluated once on a 316-patient held-out set. Decision curves used the held-out set only.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median tumor proportion score was 12 percent and median burden 7.4 mutations per megabase. Correlation between measures was minimal overall and within each disease. Response rates by quadrant were 51 percent (both high), 27 percent (high score, low burden), 24 percent (low score, high burden) and 8 percent (both low). Adding burden to a model containing score improved the held-out area under the curve from 0.63 to 0.70. Progression-free survival showed the same ordering, with median 11.4, 5.9, 5.2 and 2.4 months across quadrants. Among 118 mismatch repair deficient tumors, burden was uniformly high and response was 48 percent regardless of ligand score, and excluding them attenuated but did not abolish the burden effect. Calibration of the combined model was adequate (Hosmer-Lemeshow p equals 0.41).

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Two assays that are frequently treated as substitutes are in fact nearly orthogonal, and using them together identifies a group with a response rate six times that of the double-negative group. The discordant groups are large, together comprising 44 percent of the cohort, which explains much of the apparent inconsistency in single-assay literature. Our results depend on central generation of both assays from a single block, and we note that panel-based burden estimation carries measurement error that biases associations toward the null, so the true contribution of the antigenic axis is likely larger than estimated here. The analysis is retrospective and restricted to four diseases; prospective evaluation of the locked combined rule is required before it should influence treatment assignment.

title: Durable responses to pembrolizumab in mismatch repair deficient tumors of eleven histologies: a multicenter cohort

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We report outcomes for 233 patients with mismatch repair deficient or microsatellite instability high tumors of eleven histologies treated with pembrolizumab outside colorectal cancer registration studies. The objective response rate was 41.6 percent (95 percent CI 35.2 to 48.2), including 12.9 percent complete responses, and was similar across gastrointestinal, endometrial, biliary and small bowel primaries. Median progression-free survival was 16.8 months and median overall survival was not reached at 28 months of follow-up. Responses were durable, with 78 percent of responders progression-free at 24 months. Deficiency identified by immunohistochemistry for MLH1, MSH2, MSH6 and PMS2 and by a next-generation sequencing microsatellite classifier agreed in 218 of 233 cases (93.6 percent). Truncating B2M alterations were present in 18 percent of tumors and were enriched among non-responders (33 versus 8 percent, p equals 0.002). Ligand tumor proportion score did not predict response in this population.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Deficiency of the mismatch repair system produces tumors carrying large numbers of insertion and deletion events at repetitive tracts, which generate frameshifted reading frames and therefore protein sequences absent from the normal proteome. These tumors respond to PD-1 blockade at rates far exceeding those of repair-proficient disease, an observation first established in colorectal cancer and then extended in small series across other primaries. Two questions remained: whether the effect size is consistent outside the diseases in which deficiency is common, and whether the assays used to identify deficiency agree well enough for tissue-agnostic use. Analytical work comparing sequencing-based classifiers with the historical polymerase chain reaction standard had reported discordance concentrated in tumors with low neoplastic cellularity. We assembled a multicenter cohort to address both questions.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients treated between 2015 and 2019 at six centers were identified from institutional registries; eligibility required documented deficiency by immunohistochemistry, polymerase chain reaction, or a sequencing classifier, and at least one dose of pembrolizumab. Central pathology review confirmed deficiency in all cases with available tissue. Sequencing used a 468-gene panel with matched normal, providing microsatellite scores, variant counts and B2M status. Response was assessed by RECIST 1.1 with independent radiology review in 164 cases. Assay agreement was summarized with Cohen kappa and discordant cases were reviewed for neoplastic cellularity. Survival was estimated by Kaplan-Meier with Cox models adjusted for histology, line of therapy and performance status.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Responses occurred in 97 of 233 patients, with rates of 44 percent in colorectal, 47 percent in endometrial, 33 percent in biliary and 40 percent in gastric primaries; differences across histology were not significant. Median duration of response was not reached. Variant counts were uniformly elevated (median 38 per megabase) and did not further stratify response within the cohort. Assay agreement was 93.6 percent (kappa 0.79), with 11 of 15 discordant cases having neoplastic cellularity below 30 percent. Truncating B2M alterations were present in 42 tumors and were strongly enriched among patients with progressive disease as best response. Ligand score was not associated with response (odds ratio 1.06 per tenfold increase). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related toxicity occurred in 14 percent.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Tissue-agnostic use of PD-1 blockade in repair-deficient tumors is supported across histologies, with a response rate near 42 percent and durable disease control in most responders. The enrichment of truncating alterations in the obligate light chain of the class I complex among non-responders identifies the dominant escape route in this population and suggests that a simple immunohistochemical test could refine selection further. That assays disagree in roughly one case in fifteen, concentrated in low-cellularity specimens, argues for reflex confirmatory testing rather than reliance on a single method. Limitations include retrospective assembly, heterogeneity in prior therapy, and the absence of a repair-proficient comparator treated identically, which precludes formal estimation of the predictive as opposed to prognostic contribution of deficiency.

title: T cell clones shared between tumor and inflamed tissue in patients developing colitis and dermatitis on combination checkpoint therapy

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We performed deep TCR beta sequencing on paired pre-treatment tumor and affected-tissue biopsies from 88 patients who developed grade 2 or higher colitis (n equals 52) or dermatitis (n equals 36) during nivolumab plus ipilimumab. Clones occupying at least 0.5 percent of the tumor repertoire were also detected in the inflamed tissue in 41 percent of colitis cases and 22 percent of dermatitis cases, both exceeding a permuted null (p less than 0.001). Shared-clone frequency was bimodal: 34 patients had substantial sharing (median 7.9 percent of the inflamed-tissue repertoire) and 54 had essentially none. Patients with substantial sharing had higher objective response rates (62 versus 31 percent, p equals 0.004) and did not differ in toxicity severity. Stool 16S rRNA amplicon profiles at baseline differed between the two groups, with lower Faecalibacterium and higher Bacteroides fragilis relative abundance in the non-sharing group.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Toxicity from combination checkpoint therapy is widely assumed to be the inevitable price of efficacy, a belief that shapes management toward uniform and maximal immunosuppression. The assumption rests largely on the observation that toxicity and response are both more frequent with combination than with single-agent therapy, which is weak evidence for a shared mechanism at the level of individual patients. If some events are driven by clones that also recognize tumor while others reflect unmasking of unrelated autoreactive cells or bystander cytokine injury, then management could be differentiated. Retrospective analyses had previously reported that antibiotic exposure before therapy is associated with inferior survival and with altered intestinal communities, suggesting a second axis that could modify both endpoints. We tested clonal relatedness directly.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients with advanced melanoma or renal cell carcinoma at four centers underwent endoscopic or skin biopsy within 72 hours of event onset, before systemic immunosuppression where feasible; 71 of 88 met that criterion and a sensitivity analysis excluded the remainder. Pre-treatment tumor blocks were retrieved for all patients. TCR beta sequencing targeted 500000 templates per sample with a synthetic spike-in for clonality normalization. Shared-clone frequency was defined as the fraction of the inflamed-tissue repertoire occupied by clones present above 0.5 percent in tumor, and compared against a null generated by permuting patient labels 10000 times. Unaffected tissue from the same patient served as a within-subject control in 39 cases. Stool collected before the first dose was profiled by 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing. Toxicity was graded by CTCAE version 5 by a blinded committee.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Sharing exceeded the permuted null in both tissues and was substantially higher in colon than skin. The distribution across patients was clearly bimodal by mixture modeling (Bayesian information criterion favoring two components by 41 units). High-sharing patients had a 62 percent objective response rate versus 31 percent in low-sharing patients, and time to toxicity onset was shorter (median 4.1 versus 7.6 weeks). Severity, duration and steroid requirement did not differ. In unaffected tissue from the same patients, shared clones were present at one-tenth the frequency, arguing against passive circulation. Baseline stool profiles differed by sharing group, with a 2.3-fold lower relative abundance of Faecalibacterium in the low-sharing group. Serum IL-6 at onset was higher in low-sharing patients (median 42 versus 11 picograms per milliliter).

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Toxicity on combination checkpoint therapy comprises at least two mechanistically distinct entities that are clinically indistinguishable at the bedside. In roughly 40 percent of colitis cases the infiltrating repertoire overlaps substantially with the tumor repertoire, and those patients respond better; in the majority it does not, and those patients show a cytokine-dominant profile with elevated IL-6. Prior work reporting that antibiotic exposure before therapy is associated with inferior outcome fits the second group, whose baseline communities were depleted of butyrate producers. The therapeutic implication is that cytokine-directed rather than lymphocyte-depleting management may be appropriate for the non-sharing group. This study cannot establish causality, sampling is limited to a single site per patient, and the bimodality we observe requires replication in an independent cohort.

title: Cumulative corticosteroid exposure but not infliximab is associated with inferior outcome after treatment of checkpoint inhibitor colitis

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Among 604 patients with melanoma or renal cell carcinoma who developed grade 2 or higher colitis on nivolumab plus ipilimumab, 512 received corticosteroids alone and 92 received corticosteroids plus infliximab or vedolizumab. In multivariable analysis adjusted for baseline prognostic factors and for colitis severity, cumulative prednisone-equivalent exposure above 3000 milligrams within 60 days was associated with shorter overall survival (hazard ratio 1.54, 95 percent CI 1.18 to 2.01), whereas receipt of a biologic agent was not (hazard ratio 0.94). Patients escalated to a biologic within seven days of symptom onset had lower total steroid exposure (median 1840 versus 4120 milligrams) and numerically better survival. Objective response rates were 47 percent in the low-steroid group and 34 percent in the high-steroid group. Findings were consistent in a propensity-matched subset and in an analysis restricted to patients whose colitis began after documented radiographic response.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Colitis is the most frequent serious immune-related adverse event of combination checkpoint therapy, and its management is dominated by high-dose systemic corticosteroids, escalating to tumor necrosis factor or integrin blockade only after failure. This sequence was established empirically and has never been compared prospectively, and it carries an obvious theoretical cost, since corticosteroids deplete and functionally silence the same lymphocyte populations that mediate tumor control. Recent work showed that colitis in this setting comprises at least two entities, one in which the infiltrating repertoire overlaps substantially with the tumor repertoire and one in which it does not, with the former group responding at 62 versus 31 percent. If that distinction is real, then blanket lymphocyte-directed immunosuppression should be more costly in some patients than in others. We examined outcomes as a function of the immunosuppression actually delivered.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: We assembled a retrospective cohort from seven centers of patients treated between 2015 and 2020 who developed adjudicated grade 2 or higher colitis. Steroid exposure was abstracted from pharmacy and infusion records and converted to prednisone equivalents; biologic exposure was recorded with timing relative to symptom onset. Landmark analysis at day 60 was used to avoid immortal time bias, and the primary analysis was a Cox model with cumulative steroid dose as a continuous variable adjusted for lactate dehydrogenase, performance status, line of therapy, disease, colitis grade and time to onset. Propensity score matching on those covariates produced 88 matched pairs. Sensitivity analyses restricted the cohort to patients with a documented response before colitis onset.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median cumulative exposure was 2960 milligrams. Above the 3000 milligram threshold, the adjusted hazard ratio for death was 1.54 and for progression 1.41. Biologic receipt was not associated with either endpoint, and early escalation was associated with a 55 percent reduction in total steroid exposure. In the propensity-matched analysis the steroid association was preserved (hazard ratio 1.49). Among 214 patients with available peripheral blood, high steroid exposure was associated with a 62 percent reduction in the frequency of TCF7-positive CD8 cells at week 12 and with contraction of tumor-associated clones detected before treatment. The blood ratio of CD8 to FOXP3-positive CD4 cells, which had risen 2.8-fold after the first ipilimumab dose, returned to pretreatment values in heavily steroid-exposed patients but was sustained in the others. Colitis recurrence after taper occurred in 22 percent of steroid-only patients versus 9 percent of biologic-treated patients. Infection requiring hospitalization occurred in 17 versus 12 percent.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: These data support earlier escalation to targeted immunosuppression as a steroid-sparing strategy rather than as a rescue measure. The observed contraction of the self-renewing CD8 compartment under heavy steroid exposure provides a plausible mechanism for the survival association and links a management decision to a cell population known to be required for benefit. The finding is consistent with, and extends, the demonstration that a subset of colitis is driven by clones shared with the tumor, since indiscriminate lymphocyte suppression would be expected to harm precisely that subset. Confounding by indication is the principal threat to validity here: sicker patients receive more steroids. Propensity matching and the response-restricted sensitivity analysis mitigate but cannot eliminate this concern, and a randomized comparison is warranted.

title: Two cycles of preoperative nivolumab with low-dose ipilimumab in resectable stage III melanoma: residual viable tumor and immune correlates

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Sixty patients with resectable stage IIIB or IIIC melanoma received two cycles of nivolumab 3 mg/kg with ipilimumab 1 mg/kg before lymphadenectomy (NCT04205552). Ten percent or less residual viable tumor was observed in 34 of 58 evaluable resection specimens (58.6 percent, 95 percent CI 44.9 to 71.4), including 22 with no residual viable tumor. At a median follow-up of 27 months, recurrence-free survival at two years was 96 percent among patients meeting the ten percent threshold and 41 percent among those who did not. Grade 3 or higher toxicity occurred in 20 percent, and surgery was delayed beyond six weeks in three patients. Intratumoral FOXP3-positive CD4 cells fell by a median of 61 percent between baseline and resection, while the CD8 to FOXP3 ratio rose 3.4-fold; the magnitude of that shift was greater in patients meeting the threshold.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Preoperative delivery of checkpoint blockade exposes the drug to an intact primary lesion and its draining nodes and yields a specimen in which the extent of tumor destruction can be quantified directly. Early experience with combined PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade at metastatic-setting doses produced deep tissue responses but unacceptable toxicity, motivating attenuated dosing. A related question is which features of the baseline tumor predict deep responses. Prior work in melanoma and sarcoma established that organized lymphoid aggregates containing B cell follicles identify patients likely to benefit from checkpoint blockade, with response rates of 51 versus 18 percent, and suggested that these structures function as a niche for less differentiated lymphocytes. Whether the same feature predicts tissue-level response in the preoperative setting is unknown.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Eligible patients had palpable, biopsy-proven stage IIIB or IIIC disease and no prior systemic therapy. Two cycles were given three weeks apart with surgery targeted at week six. Resection specimens were assessed centrally by two dermatopathologists using published criteria for residual viable tumor, with blinded adjudication. Baseline core biopsies and resection specimens were analyzed by a twelve-marker multiplex panel with automated segmentation and by bulk RNA sequencing. Aggregate presence was scored on baseline specimens by the previously published binary rule. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with ten percent or less residual viable tumor; the trial was designed to reject a null rate of 35 percent with 90 percent power. Toxicity used CTCAE version 5.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Of 58 evaluable specimens, 22 had no residual viable tumor, 12 had one to ten percent, 9 had 11 to 50 percent and 15 had more than 50 percent. Two-year recurrence-free survival was 96 versus 41 percent by threshold. Grade 3 or higher toxicity occurred in 12 patients, most commonly hepatitis and colitis; no grade 5 events occurred. Baseline aggregate presence was associated with meeting the threshold (76 versus 43 percent, p equals 0.01). Intratumoral FOXP3-positive CD4 cells declined markedly by resection while CD8 numbers rose, and the change in ratio was larger in patients meeting the threshold (5.1-fold versus 1.9-fold). Bulk profiling showed induction of CXCL9, GZMB and HLA-DRA. Circulating tumor DNA was undetectable at week three in 29 of 34 patients meeting the threshold.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Attenuated CTLA-4 dosing preserved deep tissue responses in nearly six of ten patients while limiting grade 3 or higher toxicity to 20 percent, roughly half the rate reported with metastatic-setting dosing. The tissue data are consistent with a mechanism involving elimination of FOXP3-positive cells within the tumor rather than blockade alone, since the compartment contracted sharply within six weeks while conventional CD4 numbers were stable. The observation that baseline organized lymphoid aggregates, previously shown to identify responders in metastatic melanoma and sarcoma, also predict deep tissue response here supports their use as a stratification factor in future preoperative trials. Limitations include single-arm design, modest sample size, and follow-up too short to characterize late recurrence.

title: Plasma tumor DNA clearance by day 21 anticipates deep tissue response to preoperative pembrolizumab in resectable non-small cell lung cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Ninety-four patients with stage IB to IIIA non-small cell lung cancer received two cycles of pembrolizumab before resection. Ten percent or less residual viable tumor was observed in 27 of 89 evaluable specimens (30.3 percent). Patient-specific multiplex PCR panels tracking 16 to 30 somatic variants detected tumor DNA in plasma at baseline in 71 of 94 patients (75.5 percent); among these, clearance by day 21 occurred in 24 patients and predicted the tissue outcome with sensitivity 0.81 and specificity 0.89 (area under the curve 0.87). PD-L1 tumor proportion score of 50 percent or higher was associated with the tissue outcome but with lower discrimination (area under the curve 0.68). Combining the two measures did not significantly improve on plasma clearance alone. Two-year recurrence-free survival was 92 percent in patients with day-21 clearance versus 58 percent without.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: The interval between the first preoperative dose and surgery is short, and there is currently no way to know during that interval whether a patient is responding. An early blood-based readout would allow non-responders to proceed promptly to surgery or to switch strategy, and would provide an intermediate endpoint for regimen selection. Preoperative combination therapy in melanoma achieved ten percent or less residual viable tumor in 58.6 percent of patients using attenuated CTLA-4 dosing, with two-year recurrence-free survival of 96 percent in those meeting the threshold, establishing that tissue response carries prognostic weight. Whether a plasma assay can anticipate that endpoint in lung cancer, where shedding is lower in early-stage disease, has not been established with an assay sensitive enough to make absence of signal interpretable.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients received pembrolizumab 200 milligrams on day 1 and day 22 with surgery at week six. Plasma was collected at baseline, day 8, day 21 and preoperatively. Patient-specific panels were designed from tumor whole-exome data and applied with a limit of detection of 0.005 percent variant allele fraction, with a minimum of two informative variants required for a positive call and error suppression by unique molecular identifiers. Resection specimens were scored centrally by two pathologists for residual viable tumor with blinded adjudication. PD-L1 was scored with the 22C3 clone. Discrimination was compared by DeLong test; the day-21 timepoint was prespecified as primary and other timepoints were exploratory. Recurrence-free survival used Kaplan-Meier estimation with landmark at surgery.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Baseline detection was 61 percent in stage IB, 78 percent in stage II and 91 percent in stage IIIA. Among detectable patients, 24 cleared by day 21. Sensitivity and specificity for the tissue endpoint were 0.81 and 0.89, with positive predictive value 0.79 and negative predictive value 0.90. Discrimination at day 8 was lower (area under the curve 0.71). Ligand score of 50 percent or higher had an area under the curve of 0.68, and the combined model did not improve on plasma alone (DeLong p equals 0.34). Among 23 patients with no baseline detection, the tissue endpoint rate was 39 percent, similar to the overall cohort. Two-year recurrence-free survival was 92 versus 58 percent by clearance status, and clearance remained prognostic after adjustment for the tissue endpoint.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: A sufficiently sensitive plasma assay identifies deep tissue response three weeks into preoperative therapy, well before surgery, and does so better than the ligand assay used for selection. The prognostic information carried by clearance is partly independent of the tissue endpoint, suggesting that the two measures capture different aspects of disease control. Our results parallel the melanoma experience with attenuated combination dosing, where nearly six in ten patients achieved the tissue endpoint and recurrence was rare in that group, but the lower rate in lung cancer with single-agent therapy leaves more room for an early triage decision. The main limitations are the 24 percent of patients with no detectable baseline signal, in whom the approach is uninformative, and the single-arm design.

title: TCF7-positive CD8 cells are the proliferative source of the response to PD-1 blockade and reside in peritumoral lymphoid niches

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: In tumors from 122 patients receiving pembrolizumab or nivolumab and in three mouse models, CD8 cells segregated into a TCF7-positive SLAMF6-positive subset with low granzyme content and a TCF7-negative CD39-positive TIM-3-positive subset with high cytolytic capacity but no proliferative response to PD-1 blockade. In vivo labeling showed that essentially all post-treatment proliferation originated from the TCF7-positive subset, which gave rise to the cytolytic subset but not the converse. Baseline frequency of the TCF7-positive subset predicted objective response (odds ratio 2.4 per doubling, area under the curve 0.75), whereas total CD8 density did not (area under the curve 0.58). Multiplexed imaging localized TCF7-positive cells within CD20-rich peritumoral aggregates containing CD21-positive stromal networks, at 6.8-fold the density found within tumor nests. Conditional Tox deletion after tumor establishment expanded the subset and doubled the fraction of animals achieving durable rejection.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: PD-1 blockade is often described as reversing the dysfunction of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, but the cellular target of the antibody has not been defined in human tumors. Work in chronic viral infection established that the proliferative burst after blockade derives from a small subset retaining transcription factor 7 expression, while terminally differentiated cells do not divide. Whether the same architecture holds in cancer, where antigen exposure and tissue context differ, has been inferred rather than demonstrated. A parallel clinical literature had shown that an 18-gene chemokine and cytotoxicity signature measured before treatment predicts response with an area under the curve near 0.73 across histologies, but bulk measures cannot distinguish a large population of inert cells from a small population of competent ones. We therefore combined state-resolved human profiling with lineage tracing in mice.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Fresh human tumors were analyzed by 28-color spectral flow cytometry with paired alpha and beta chain sequencing on sorted subsets, and by single-cell RNA sequencing on 46 specimens. Mouse experiments used MC38, B16-F10 and a tamoxifen-inducible Tox conditional allele crossed to Cd8a-CreERT2, with deletion induced seven days after implantation. In vivo proliferation was measured by BrdU pulse and by fate mapping with a Tcf7-CreERT2 reporter. Multiplexed imaging used a 24-marker panel with neighborhood enrichment tested against a permuted spatial null. Response association used logistic regression adjusted for disease, line of therapy and prior treatment. Mouse groups contained ten animals; growth was analyzed by mixed-effects models and survival by log-rank test with investigators blinded to genotype.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: The TCF7-positive subset constituted a median of 5.1 percent of tumor CD8 cells (interquartile range 2.2 to 9.4). After therapy, 91 percent of BrdU incorporation in mice occurred in fate-mapped progeny of this subset. Human baseline frequency predicted response with an area under the curve of 0.75 and remained significant after adjustment for the bulk cytotoxicity signature. Imaging placed 71 percent of TCF7-positive cells within 120 micrometers of a CD20-rich aggregate. Tumor-reactive clones identified by post-treatment expansion were present in the TCF7-positive gate before treatment in 38 of 44 evaluable patients. Conditional Tox deletion increased subset frequency 2.6-fold and raised durable rejection from 20 to 50 percent of animals, while germline deletion in a parallel arm impaired subset formation entirely.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: The response to PD-1 blockade is contributed by a small, spatially restricted, self-renewing population rather than by the bulk of infiltrating lymphocytes, which explains why density-based predictors saturate at modest discrimination. Our data give a cellular interpretation to the bulk transcriptional signature that predicts response across histologies: tumors scoring high on chemokine and cytotoxicity transcripts are those most likely to contain the niche in which the competent subset survives. The finding that conditional but not germline deletion of the same transcription factor expands the subset resolves conflicting reports, since the factor is required for formation and restrains maintenance. Limitations include reliance on fresh tissue, which biases toward accessible lesions, and the possibility that fate mapping efficiency differs between subsets.

title: Allele-specific HLA loss and depletion of predicted binders indicate immune editing in lung and head and neck carcinoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Using a haplotype-aware caller validated against single-cell DNA sequencing, we detected loss of one parental HLA haplotype in 118 of 604 tumors (19.5 percent) across lung, head and neck and melanoma primaries. Loss was clonal in 79 percent of affected tumors and co-occurred with B2M alteration in only 4 percent and with inactivating JAK1 or JAK2 alterations in 2 percent, indicating largely distinct routes. Tumors with loss showed selective depletion of mutations predicted to yield peptides binding the lost allele: the observed to expected ratio of predicted binders for lost alleles was 0.71 compared with 0.98 for retained alleles (p less than 0.001), after conditioning on trinucleotide context and transcript abundance. Depletion was strongest in tumors with high cytotoxic lymphocyte infiltration. Among 260 patients subsequently treated with PD-1 blockade, haplotype loss was associated with shorter progression-free survival independent of variant count and ligand score (hazard ratio 1.68, 95 percent CI 1.19 to 2.37).

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Selection rules based on counting nonsynonymous variants assume that the resulting peptides are equally available for display. Tumors evolving under lymphocyte pressure can violate that assumption by deleting one parental haplotype, which narrows the displayed peptide space without abolishing display and therefore escapes detection by staining for the invariant light chain. Prior work established that tumors deficient in mismatch repair respond to PD-1 blockade at rates near 42 percent across histologies, but also that truncating light chain alterations are enriched among the non-responders in that population, demonstrating that display defects limit benefit even when antigenic material is abundant. Whether the subtler, allele-specific form of loss produces measurable editing of the mutational landscape and predicts outcome has been contested, largely because of methodological disagreements about how to control for mutational processes.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Whole-exome or deep panel sequencing with matched germline was available for 604 tumors from three institutional cohorts. Haplotype-aware calling used phased reads across the polymorphic region combined with allele-specific coverage and purity estimates; performance was benchmarked on in silico mixtures and on 20 tumors with orthogonal single-cell validation, achieving sensitivity 0.92 at purity above 0.4. Peptide binding was predicted with a consensus of two algorithms at a 500 nanomolar threshold. The depletion statistic compared observed binder counts with expectations from a trinucleotide context-matched mutational model weighted by transcript abundance. Survival analysis in the treated subset used Cox models with variant count, ligand score, stage and disease as covariates. Analyses were prespecified apart from the infiltration-stratified comparison.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Haplotype loss prevalence was 22 percent in lung, 19 percent in head and neck and 14 percent in melanoma. Loss was clonal in most affected tumors and rarely coincided with light chain inactivation or with JAK1 and JAK2 kinase-domain lesions, which were detected in 14 tumors overall. The observed to expected binder ratio was 0.71 for lost alleles versus 0.98 for retained alleles, and fell to 0.58 in the upper tertile of cytotoxic infiltration. Variant counts were not lower in tumors with loss, confirming that the effect is on which mutations are retained rather than how many. In the treated subset, median progression-free survival was 3.2 months with loss versus 6.9 months without, and the association held within the burden-high stratum. Adding loss status to a model containing burden and ligand score improved the concordance index from 0.61 to 0.66.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Allele-specific loss is common, clonal, associated with measurable editing of the retained mutational landscape, and predicts inferior outcome independent of the two assays used clinically. It is mechanistically distinct from complete inactivation of the invariant light chain, which was reported to be enriched among non-responders in repair-deficient disease and which abolishes display entirely rather than narrowing it. Because standard targeted panels misassign copy number in this region, the phenomenon is invisible in routine practice, and a panel-compatible caller would be required for prospective use. The main limitations are that binding prediction remains imperfect, that our depletion statistic assumes the mutational process is stationary over tumor evolution, and that the treated subset is retrospective.

title: CD73-generated adenosine in poorly perfused tumor regions silences infiltrating CD8 cells and limits PD-1 blockade

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: In 90 surgical specimens labeled preoperatively with pimonidazole, mass spectrometry imaging showed adenosine concentrations 4.6-fold higher in labeled regions than in adjacent perfused regions, colocalizing with NT5E-positive stroma and CD11b-positive cells. CD8 cells within labeled regions were present at equivalent density but showed 68 percent lower granzyme B and 74 percent lower TNF staining. In MC38 and B16-F10, conditional Nt5e deletion in CD11b-positive cells reduced intratumoral adenosine by 61 percent whereas deletion in tumor cells reduced it by 22 percent, identifying the phagocyte compartment as the dominant source. Adoptive transfer of Adora2a-deficient OT-I cells restored granule release within labeled regions. A2A receptor antagonism combined with anti-PD-1 produced complete rejection in 7 of 12 MC38-bearing mice versus 1 of 12 with anti-PD-1 alone, and low-dose anti-VEGFR2 reproduced most of the benefit while raising measured intratumoral oxygen tension.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Lymphocytes that are present in a tumor but functionally silent are frequently attributed to checkpoint receptor engagement, yet blockade of those receptors restores function in only a minority of patients. An alternative explanation is that the physical and chemical conditions of the tumor bed impose constraints that no receptor antibody can relieve. Regions distant from perfused vessels accumulate extracellular ATP catabolites through sequential ectoenzymatic hydrolysis, and signaling through the A2A receptor raises cyclic AMP and suppresses granule exocytosis. Prior work had shown that the population capable of responding to PD-1 blockade is a small self-renewing subset with defined spatial preferences, which raises the possibility that metabolic constraints act by eliminating the niches those cells require. We mapped metabolite concentration and lymphocyte function in registered coordinates.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Ninety patients undergoing resection received pimonidazole 500 milligrams per square meter 16 hours preoperatively. Serial sections were used for mass spectrometry imaging at 30-micrometer resolution, for pimonidazole immunohistochemistry, and for a 12-marker multiplex panel; sections were registered by affine transformation with landmark validation. Marker intensity was modeled against distance to the labeled boundary with mixed-effects regression accounting for patient. Mouse work used Nt5e conditional alleles crossed to Lyz2-Cre, Fsp1-Cre or tumor-cell deletion, with eight to ten animals per arm. Intratumoral oxygen tension was measured with a fiber-optic probe before and 72 hours after low-dose anti-VEGFR2. Growth was analyzed with mixed-effects models and survival by log-rank; tumor measurement was blinded.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Adenosine was 4.6-fold enriched in labeled regions, and lactate 2.9-fold, with interstitial pH 0.4 units lower. CD8 density did not differ between labeled and perfused regions, but granzyme B and TNF intensity fell steeply with distance into the labeled zone (26 percent decrease per 100 micrometers). NT5E signal was strongest on CD11b-positive cells and on alpha-smooth muscle actin-positive stroma. Compartment-specific deletion identified the phagocyte source as dominant. Transfer of receptor-deficient OT-I cells restored degranulation within labeled regions to 84 percent of the perfused-region level. Combination of A2A antagonism with anti-PD-1 rejected 7 of 12 tumors; anti-VEGFR2 raised measured oxygen tension from 4.1 to 11.6 millimeters of mercury and rejected 5 of 12. Ectoenzyme staining intensity above the locked threshold identified the models that benefited.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Functional silencing of infiltrating lymphocytes is spatially organized and tracks with a measurable metabolite gradient rather than with cell density, which explains why density-based biomarkers fail to identify these tumors. That the dominant enzymatic source is the phagocyte compartment rather than the tumor cell has direct consequences for drug selection, favoring approaches that remove or reprogram those cells over direct enzymatic inhibition. The result also connects to the finding that the cells responsible for the response to PD-1 blockade occupy specific peritumoral niches: metabolic constraint is concentrated precisely in the regions those cells do not inhabit. Limitations include the use of a single labeling agent as a surrogate for oxygen tension in human tissue, and the possibility that registration error across serial sections attenuates the measured gradients.

title: Antibiotic exposure before PD-1 blockade and intestinal community composition in 512 patients with melanoma or lung cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We prospectively enrolled 512 patients starting pembrolizumab or nivolumab and banked stool before the first dose. Systemic antibiotics within 30 days before treatment were documented in 148 patients (28.9 percent). After inverse probability weighting for confounding by indication, antibiotic exposure was associated with shorter overall survival (hazard ratio 1.61, 95 percent CI 1.24 to 2.09) and lower objective response (22 versus 38 percent). Shotgun metagenomic profiling showed higher relative abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and greater pathway abundance for short-chain fatty acid production in responders. A locked eleven-taxon score derived in 300 patients discriminated response in the remaining 212 with an area under the curve of 0.67. Transfer of communities from four responders and four non-responders into germ-free mice reproduced the phenotype, with recipient tumors under anti-PD-1 growing 2.4-fold faster in non-responder recipients.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Multiple retrospective series have reported that antibiotic exposure around the start of checkpoint blockade is associated with inferior outcome, but the reported magnitude varies widely and the taxa said to distinguish responders differ from study to study. Two design features plausibly account for the inconsistency: confounding by the indication for which antibiotics were prescribed, since infection is itself a marker of poor prognosis, and reliance on amplicon profiling that resolves neither strain identity nor metabolic capacity. Meanwhile, tissue-based selection assays have advanced substantially, and a central comparison of ligand immunohistochemistry with mutational burden showed that the two together identify a group responding at 51 percent versus 8 percent for the double-negative group, setting a benchmark that any host-factor marker should be judged against.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients at four centers were enrolled before their first dose. Stool was self-collected into stabilizing buffer at baseline, week 6 and week 12. Antibiotic exposure was abstracted from pharmacy records and adjudicated by two reviewers blinded to outcome, with indication recorded. Shotgun sequencing targeted 20 million paired reads with strain-level profiling and pathway quantification. The primary analysis used inverse probability of treatment weighting with covariates including performance status, corticosteroid use, prior lines, lactate dehydrogenase and infection indication. A taxon score was derived by penalized regression in a locked 300-patient training set. Germ-free C57BL/6 mice were colonized by oral gavage two weeks before MC38 implantation, eight animals per donor, with anti-PD-1 from day 7.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Exposure was most often to beta-lactams and fluoroquinolones, prescribed predominantly for respiratory and urinary indications. Weighted analysis gave a hazard ratio of 1.61 for death and 1.44 for progression; the association was stronger for exposure within 14 days than for 15 to 30 days. Responders had 3.1-fold higher relative abundance of A. muciniphila and higher butyrate synthesis pathway abundance. The locked score achieved an area under the curve of 0.67 in validation, compared with 0.62 for ligand score in the same patients. In germ-free recipients, tumors in non-responder-colonized mice grew faster under anti-PD-1 and contained fewer granzyme B-positive CD8 cells and a 2.2-fold higher fraction of Trem2-high phagocytes. Grade 2 or higher colitis was more frequent in responder-colonized recipients of a reciprocal transfer experiment.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Prospective collection with explicit adjustment for the indication for antibiotics preserves an association of clinically meaningful size, which addresses the principal objection to prior retrospective reports. The discriminative performance of a locked community score is modest and comparable to that of ligand immunohistochemistry alone; it falls well short of the combined tissue assay benchmark reported for immunohistochemistry with mutational burden, and it should be regarded as complementary rather than competitive. The transfer experiments support causality but use a small number of donors, and the mouse phenotype includes a shift in the phagocyte compartment that we did not anticipate and that requires independent confirmation. Clinically, the immediate implication is stewardship: avoiding unnecessary broad-spectrum agents in the month before therapy is a no-cost intervention.

title: Analytical concordance of four PD-L1 immunohistochemistry assays and interobserver agreement across 28 pathologists

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We compared the 22C3, 28-8, SP263 and SP142 assays on serial sections from 120 non-small cell lung carcinoma resection blocks, each stained in three laboratories, and had 28 pathologists score tumor proportion score on digitized slides. Analytical concordance among 22C3, 28-8 and SP263 was high (pairwise Lin concordance correlation coefficient 0.87 to 0.91), while SP142 stained tumor cells substantially less intensely, yielding a median tumor proportion score 14 percentage points lower. Interobserver agreement for tumor cell scoring was substantial (intraclass correlation 0.83) but fell markedly for immune cell scoring (0.19). At the 1 percent cut point, 22C3 and SP142 assigned different categories in 27 percent of cases; at the 50 percent cut point, discordance was 12 percent. Repeat staining of the same block in different laboratories introduced a median absolute difference of 6 percentage points.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Four immunohistochemical assays for the same protein were developed alongside four different antibodies and registered with different scoring algorithms and cut points. Clinicians and trialists nonetheless treat the resulting scores as a single continuous variable, comparing values across studies and applying cut points derived with one assay to results generated with another. Whether that practice is analytically defensible is an assay validation question, distinct from the clinical question of how well any of these assays predicts benefit. Prior comparisons have been limited by small case numbers, single-laboratory staining, or scoring by a handful of readers, none of which supports an estimate of the variance components that matter in routine practice. We designed a study to partition variance across assay, laboratory and reader.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: One hundred twenty resection blocks with tumor content above 40 percent were sectioned serially and distributed to three accredited laboratories, each of which ran all four assays on their own platforms using validated protocols. Slides were digitized at 40-fold magnification. Twenty-eight pathologists from 14 institutions, each with at least two years of thoracic experience, scored tumor proportion score and immune cell score after a standardized training module. Agreement was quantified with intraclass correlation coefficients and Lin concordance correlation, and categorical agreement at 1 percent and 50 percent cut points with Cohen kappa. A mixed-effects model partitioned variance into assay, laboratory, reader and residual components. No clinical outcome data were used.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median tumor proportion score across blocks was 22 percent with 22C3, 24 percent with 28-8, 21 percent with SP263 and 8 percent with SP142. Pairwise concordance among the first three assays exceeded 0.87. Categorical discordance between 22C3 and SP142 was 27 percent at the 1 percent cut point. Reader variance accounted for 9 percent of total variance for tumor cell scoring but 46 percent for immune cell scoring. Laboratory contributed 4 percent and assay 31 percent. Kappa for the 50 percent cut point across the three concordant assays was 0.79. Readers with higher case volume were not more concordant. Rescoring a random 20 percent of slides after eight weeks gave an intra-reader intraclass correlation of 0.88.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Three of the four assays are analytically interchangeable for tumor cell scoring within the precision limits established here, and one is not. Immune cell scoring is not reproducible enough for clinical use without substantial protocol change, a finding with implications for any algorithm that incorporates it. These are measurement properties only. Nothing in this study addresses whether any assay identifies patients who benefit from therapy, which requires outcome data and a different design; our results simply bound the measurement error that such studies inherit. The practical recommendation is that cut points be applied only with the assay from which they were derived, and that immune cell scoring be reported with explicit uncertainty or replaced by an automated method.

title: Panel size, filtering strategy and germline subtraction determine the variance of tumor mutational burden estimates

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We evaluated tumor mutational burden estimates from in silico downsampling of 1580 whole exomes to panel footprints between 0.2 and 3.0 megabases, and from empirical sequencing of 214 specimens on three commercial panels. Estimates from footprints below 0.8 megabases showed a coefficient of variation above 30 percent at true burdens near the commonly used 10 mutations per megabase threshold, producing categorical misclassification in 22 percent of specimens. Omitting matched germline subtraction inflated estimates by a median of 2.9 mutations per megabase, with inflation greatest in individuals of non-European genetic ancestry (median 4.6 versus 2.1, p less than 0.001). Including synonymous variants reduced variance but shifted absolute values, requiring panel-specific recalibration. Deconvolving clonal hematopoiesis variants changed estimates by more than 1 mutation per megabase in 8 percent of specimens. We provide calibration curves mapping panel estimates onto exome-equivalent values.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Mutational burden is reported as a single number and compared against a common threshold, yet the number is produced by pipelines that differ in captured footprint, variant filtering, germline handling and normalization. The measurement properties of these pipelines have received far less scrutiny than their clinical associations, with the result that thresholds derived on one assay are routinely applied to values generated by another. This is an analytical validation problem, and answering it requires no outcome data at all. Similar variance-partitioning work in immunohistochemistry has shown that assay identity can account for a third of total variance in a protein score, and that categorical agreement at clinically used cut points is considerably worse than continuous agreement suggests. We conducted the analogous study for sequencing-derived burden.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Whole-exome data from 1580 tumors across twelve histologies with matched germline, of which non-small cell lung carcinoma was the most frequent at 402 specimens, were downsampled in silico to 40 synthetic panel footprints spanning 0.2 to 3.0 megabases, with 200 random gene sets per footprint size. Empirical comparison used 214 specimens sequenced on three commercial panels and on whole exome in a single laboratory. Germline subtraction was compared against population-database filtering at three allele frequency thresholds, stratified by inferred genetic ancestry. Clonal hematopoiesis variants were identified by matched blood sequencing. Variance was partitioned by mixed-effects modeling, and calibration curves were fit by isotonic regression with bootstrap confidence bands. No patient outcomes were analyzed and no clinical claims are made.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Coefficient of variation at a true burden of 10 mutations per megabase was 41 percent for a 0.4 megabase footprint, 28 percent at 0.8 megabases and 14 percent at 2.0 megabases. Categorical misclassification against the exome reference was 22 percent for small panels. Database-only filtering inflated estimates by 2.9 mutations per megabase overall, and by 4.6 in individuals with non-European ancestry, reflecting reference database composition. Including synonymous variants reduced the coefficient of variation by roughly a quarter at every footprint. Clonal hematopoiesis contributed materially in 8 percent of specimens, concentrated in older patients. Empirical panel results agreed with the downsampling predictions within confidence bands. Specimens with mismatch repair deficiency were classified above threshold by every footprint tested and contributed no misclassification, so the variance problem is confined to the middle of the distribution. Isotonic calibration reduced median absolute error from 3.4 to 1.2 mutations per megabase.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Burden estimates from small panels carry enough measurement error to misclassify roughly one specimen in five at commonly used thresholds, and the error is not symmetric across ancestry groups when matched germline is unavailable. These are properties of the measurement, and the paper makes no claim about which patients benefit from therapy; that question requires outcome data and randomized comparison. The ancestry-dependent inflation is the most consequential finding for equity, since it systematically pushes one group above thresholds used to grant access to treatment. Calibration curves of the kind we provide are a partial remedy but do not substitute for matched germline sequencing. Laboratories reporting burden should publish their footprint, filtering rules and calibration, none of which is currently standard.

title: Population pharmacokinetics of nivolumab and exposure-response for a 480 mg every four weeks flat dosing regimen

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We developed a population pharmacokinetic model from 3721 patients receiving nivolumab across nine studies in melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer and renal cell carcinoma, comprising 21489 serum concentration observations. A two-compartment model with time-varying clearance described the data; clearance decreased by a median of 24 percent from baseline to steady state, with the magnitude of decrease correlated with tumor response. Body weight, sex, performance status, baseline albumin and estimated glomerular filtration rate were significant covariates, but none produced exposure changes exceeding 20 percent within the observed range. Simulations showed that flat dosing at 480 milligrams every four weeks yields steady-state trough and average concentrations within 15 percent of the 3 milligrams per kilogram every two weeks regimen across the weight range 35 to 160 kilograms. Exposure-response analysis found a flat relationship for both objective response and grade 3 or higher adverse events over the fifth to ninety-fifth exposure percentile.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Weight-based dosing of monoclonal antibodies is inherited from cytotoxic chemotherapy practice and is rarely justified by the pharmacokinetics of the molecules themselves. Antibodies of this class have low clearance, long half-lives and target-mediated disposition that saturates well below therapeutic exposures, all of which argue that fixed dosing should produce acceptable exposure uniformity. Establishing this requires a population model built on a large pooled dataset with adequate representation at the extremes of body size, together with an exposure-response analysis demonstrating that the relationship is flat in the region of interest. Analytical rigor of this kind has become routine for measurement assays in this field, where variance partitioning studies have shown that assay identity can dominate reported values, and the same standard should apply to dosing decisions.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Data were pooled from nine studies with intensive and sparse sampling. Modeling used nonlinear mixed-effects estimation with first-order conditional estimation with interaction. Structural model selection compared one- and two-compartment models with constant and time-varying clearance by objective function value and visual predictive checks. Covariates were screened by stepwise inclusion at p less than 0.01 and backward elimination at p less than 0.001. Simulations of 1000 virtual patients per regimen used the final parameter estimates with the observed covariate distribution. Exposure-response used logistic regression of response and of grade 3 or higher adverse events against time-averaged concentration, with quartile plots and tests for trend. Bootstrap resampling with 500 replicates assessed parameter precision.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: The final model had clearance 9.5 milliliters per hour at baseline with a maximal 24 percent reduction over time, central volume 3.6 liters, and interindividual variability of 31 percent on clearance. Time-varying clearance improved the objective function by 1842 units. Weight was the strongest covariate, with an exponent of 0.61 on clearance. Simulated geometric mean steady-state trough was 56.2 micrograms per milliliter for flat dosing versus 51.9 for weight-based dosing, and the ratio of exposures between the lightest and heaviest deciles was 1.9 for flat dosing versus 1.4 for weight-based. Exposure-response was flat: odds ratio for objective response 1.03 per doubling of exposure and 1.08 for grade 3 or higher events, neither significant. Predictive checks showed adequate description across studies.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Fixed dosing at 480 milligrams every four weeks produces exposures comparable to weight-based dosing, and because the exposure-response relationship is flat over the relevant range, the modest increase in exposure variability at the extremes of body size carries no expected consequence for efficacy or safety. The decline in clearance over time is associated with response and most likely reflects reversal of cachexia-associated catabolism rather than any change in drug disposition; it is a confounder for naive exposure-response analysis and was handled by using time-averaged rather than early exposure. This analysis concerns dosing convenience and exposure uniformity only. It does not address which patients should receive the drug, and it provides no information about tumor biology or patient selection.

title: Cost-effectiveness of first-line pembrolizumab plus platinum doublet versus chemotherapy alone in advanced non-squamous lung cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We built a partitioned survival model with progression-free, post-progression and death states to compare first-line pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed and carboplatin against chemotherapy alone in advanced non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer, from a United States payer perspective over a lifetime horizon with 3 percent annual discounting. Base-case incremental cost was 148200 dollars for an incremental 0.72 quality-adjusted life years, giving an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of 205800 dollars per quality-adjusted life year. Restricting to patients with a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of 50 percent or higher lowered the ratio to 121400 dollars. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis showed a 22 percent probability of being cost-effective at a 150000 dollar threshold overall and 61 percent in the high-expression subgroup. Drug acquisition price and the duration of treatment beyond 24 months were the dominant drivers; adopting a four-weekly administration schedule reduced administration costs by 9 percent without altering the conclusion.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have moved to the first line in lung cancer on the strength of survival benefits that are real but heterogeneous, at prices that strain payer budgets and patient cost-sharing arrangements. Economic evaluation asks a question distinct from clinical efficacy: given a fixed budget, does adopting this regimen produce more health than the alternatives it displaces. Answering it requires survival extrapolation beyond trial follow-up, utility weights by health state, and resource use estimates, none of which are biological quantities. Biomarker stratification enters the analysis only through its effect on the survival curves and on testing costs. We therefore do not evaluate assay performance or mechanism here, and we take reported subgroup efficacy at face value while testing its influence in sensitivity analysis.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Survival curves were digitized from the pivotal trial publication and extrapolated with parametric and spline models selected by information criteria and clinical plausibility assessment by two oncologists. Costs were drawn from wholesale acquisition price, Medicare physician fee schedule and published estimates of adverse event management, inflated to 2020 dollars. Utility weights came from trial-collected EQ-5D data. The model cycle was three weeks with half-cycle correction. One-way sensitivity analysis varied each parameter across plausible ranges; probabilistic analysis used 10000 Monte Carlo draws from fitted distributions. Scenario analyses examined treatment duration caps at 12, 24 and 35 cycles, biosimilar entry, and administration every four weeks rather than every three weeks. Reporting follows the CHEERS 2022 checklist.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Modeled mean survival was 3.14 years with the immunotherapy regimen versus 2.02 years with chemotherapy alone. Incremental cost was 148200 dollars, dominated by drug acquisition (81 percent). The base-case ratio was 205800 dollars per quality-adjusted life year, falling to 121400 dollars in the high-expression subgroup and rising to 268000 dollars in the score-negative subgroup. A treatment duration cap at 24 months lowered the base-case ratio to 158900 dollars. A 40 percent price reduction would bring the base case below 150000 dollars. Acceptability curves crossed the 150000 dollar threshold at 22 percent probability overall. Results were insensitive to utility weights and to adverse event costs, which contributed under 3 percent of total spending.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: At current United States prices the regimen is not cost-effective at conventional thresholds for the unselected population, and is close to acceptable in the high-expression subgroup. The dominant lever is price, not clinical management, and the second lever is treatment duration, which is set by convention rather than evidence. Our analysis inherits all the uncertainty of extrapolating trial survival curves beyond their observed follow-up, and the confidence intervals we report understate that structural uncertainty. We emphasize that nothing in this analysis speaks to the biology of response, to the validity of the selection assay, or to which individual patient should receive treatment; those are separate questions requiring different data. The conclusions are specific to the United States payer perspective and do not transfer to systems with negotiated pricing.
