title: TREM2-high macrophages at the invasive margin predict recurrence after curative resection of hepatocellular carcinoma in patients who received no systemic therapy

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We profiled 214 hepatocellular carcinoma resection specimens from patients treated with curative-intent surgery alone, none of whom received checkpoint inhibitors or other systemic therapy, using single-cell RNA sequencing on 34 fresh specimens and multiplexed imaging on the full series. A TREM2-high APOE-high macrophage state occupied a median of 16 percent of mononuclear phagocytes and was concentrated within 100 micrometers of the invasive margin. Patients in the upper tertile of marginal density had a two-year recurrence rate of 61 percent versus 29 percent in the lower tertile (adjusted hazard ratio 2.1, 95 percent CI 1.4 to 3.2), independent of tumor size, microvascular invasion, alpha-fetoprotein and Edmondson grade. The association was strongest for early recurrence within 12 months, which is thought to reflect residual disease rather than de novo tumorigenesis. Adding marginal density to a standard clinical model improved the concordance index from 0.68 to 0.74.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Recurrence after curative resection of hepatocellular carcinoma exceeds 60 percent at five years, and existing risk models based on tumor size, number, vascular invasion and serum markers discriminate poorly. Features of the surrounding tissue, including fibrosis stage and inflammatory composition, are known to carry prognostic information that clinical variables do not capture. A conserved lipid-handling macrophage state has been described across human tumors and was reported to be enriched in patients whose disease failed to respond to PD-1 blockade, where its density at the tumor-stroma interface correlated inversely with lymphocyte penetration. Whether the same state carries prognostic weight in the entirely different clinical situation of surgically resected disease without systemic therapy has not been examined, and the two questions should not be conflated.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Consecutive patients undergoing resection between 2012 and 2019 at two centers with complete pathology and at least 24 months of follow-up or documented recurrence were included. Fresh tissue from 34 patients was dissociated within two hours for single-cell libraries targeting 6000 cells. The full series was stained with a 14-marker panel including TREM2, APOE, CD68, CD163, CD8, CD20 and pan-cytokeratin, and analyzed with automated segmentation and distance-to-margin metrics. Recurrence was defined radiologically with pathological confirmation where available and classified as early or late at a 12-month cut point. Cox models were adjusted for prespecified clinical covariates. Discrimination was compared by concordance index with bootstrap confidence intervals. No patient received immunotherapy before or after surgery.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Single-cell analysis recovered eight phagocyte states, of which the TREM2-high APOE-high state was the most abundant in tumor relative to adjacent liver (16 versus 4 percent). Imaging showed a marginal band with median width 84 micrometers. Upper-tertile marginal density was associated with two-year recurrence of 61 percent versus 29 percent, and the association was preserved after adjustment. Stratified by timing, the adjusted hazard ratio was 2.6 for early recurrence and 1.2 for late recurrence. CD8 density within tumor nests was lower in high-density cases, but adding CD8 density to the model did not attenuate the macrophage effect. Concordance improved from 0.68 to 0.74. Marginal density was not associated with fibrosis stage or with viral etiology.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: A macrophage state previously implicated in failure of checkpoint blockade also predicts early recurrence after surgery in patients who never received such therapy, which indicates that its prognostic value does not depend on an ongoing immunotherapeutic intervention. The distinction matters for interpretation: reports describing this state as a mediator of treatment failure, including the single-cell survey that first placed it at the tumor-stroma interface in checkpoint-treated patients, cannot separate a treatment-specific mechanism from a general marker of aggressive biology, and our surgical series suggests the latter contributes substantially. Limitations include the retrospective design, the restriction of single-cell profiling to a subset, and the absence of a treated comparator group within the same institution, which would be required to test the two interpretations directly.

title: Mature tertiary lymphoid structures and recurrence-free survival after complete resection of colorectal liver metastases without perioperative immunotherapy

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We graded tertiary lymphoid structures in 286 resected colorectal liver metastasis specimens from patients who received fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin-based perioperative chemotherapy but no checkpoint inhibitor. Structures were present in 132 specimens (46 percent) and contained active germinal centers in 47. Five-year recurrence-free survival was 48 percent for germinal center containing structures, 27 percent for immature structures and 24 percent for structure-negative specimens (log-rank p equals 0.002), with no difference between the latter two groups. The association was independent of the clinical risk score, RAS status and response to preoperative chemotherapy (adjusted hazard ratio 0.55, 95 percent CI 0.37 to 0.82). Only three specimens were mismatch repair deficient, so the finding is not explained by that subgroup. Structure grade was not associated with the density of CD8 cells within metastatic nodules.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Prognostic models for resected colorectal liver metastases rest on tumor number, size, nodal status of the primary, carcinoembryonic antigen and mutational status, and perform modestly. Histological features of the metastasis and its interface with liver parenchyma, including the growth pattern and the composition of the peritumoral infiltrate, add information in several series. Organized lymphoid aggregates with germinal centers have attracted attention chiefly in the context of immunotherapy, where a graded assessment in head and neck cancer showed that only structures containing active germinal centers were associated with survival after PD-1 blockade, while immature structures behaved like their absence. Whether the same threshold effect operates in a surgical population that never receives checkpoint inhibitors is a separate question that bears on whether the feature is predictive or simply prognostic.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Consecutive resections between 2010 and 2018 at three centers were reviewed; patients receiving any immune checkpoint inhibitor at any time were excluded. A seven-marker multiplex panel (CD3, CD8, CD20, CD21, Ki-67, AICDA, pan-cytokeratin) was applied to whole sections including at least 5 millimeters of adjacent liver. Grading used the same prespecified rule published for head and neck specimens, applied by two pathologists blinded to outcome with adjudication. Mismatch repair status was determined by immunohistochemistry. Recurrence-free survival was measured from resection, and Cox models were adjusted for the clinical risk score, RAS and BRAF status, number and size of metastases, and pathological response to chemotherapy. A prespecified sensitivity analysis excluded patients with fewer than 12 months of follow-up.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Structures were present in 46 percent of specimens, with germinal centers in 47 (16 percent of all specimens). Five-year recurrence-free survival was 48, 27 and 24 percent across the three grades, and the ordinal model again showed a threshold rather than a gradient. Adjusted hazard ratio for the highest grade was 0.55. Grade was concordant between two separate metastatic nodules from the same patient in 39 of 52 evaluable cases. Structure grade was not associated with intranodular CD8 density (Spearman rho 0.08) but was associated with a denser peritumoral lymphocytic rim. Interobserver agreement was substantial (Fleiss kappa 0.71). Patients with high-grade structures had similar rates of pathological response to preoperative chemotherapy, indicating the marker is not a proxy for chemosensitivity.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: The threshold effect of germinal center activity, previously demonstrated in patients receiving PD-1 blockade for head and neck carcinoma where only mature structures were associated with survival, is reproduced here in a surgical population that never received such therapy. This argues that the feature is prognostic rather than specifically predictive of benefit from checkpoint inhibition, a distinction that the immunotherapy literature has largely left untested because comparator groups treated without these agents are rarely profiled. Our study cannot exclude that the feature carries additional predictive value on top of its prognostic contribution, which would require a randomized or matched treated comparator. Limitations include retrospective design, heterogeneity of chemotherapy regimens, and the small number of mismatch repair deficient cases.
